tm.summary: BrowserStack Test Management: author and organise test cases, plan and track their execution, and report on the results. Everything is scoped to a project, which owns the folders, cases, runs, plans and reports beneath it. Search and filter cases; create and update cases, runs and plans; record results; bulk edit, move, copy, archive and delete; restructure folders; manage tags and custom-field definitions; assign, clone and close runs; review AI duplicate recommendations; read the activity feed and a case's version history; and create, schedule and download reports. Cases are authored and their outcomes recorded here, but tests are not RUN here: execution happens in your own runner or another BrowserStack product. Renaming and deleting a project are not exposed. Destructive capabilities exist and always need explicit human approval.

Identity is synchronous, data is not: the response carries the new run as soon as it exists, but its case mappings are filled in by a background worker. Reading the new run's test cases immediately can legitimately return zero rows — retry before concluding the clone was empty.

body.description: Filter criteria used to resolve cases, and the only place is_dynamic is read. is_dynamic:true needs at least one other key here or the call 400s; is_dynamic:false turns a dynamic run static. Omitting is_dynamic leaves the run's current dynamic flag alone.

body.name: configuration_map
body.description: Per-case configuration assignment overlay: each entry is {test_case_id: "TC-1" or ["TC-1","TC-2"], configuration_ids: [101,102]}. Unresolvable case or configuration IDs return 422. It is an overlay, not the case list — cases you list elsewhere are still included, with a null-configuration row.

body.name: filter_scope
body.description: Accepted by the parameter filter but NOT honoured on either update path — the selection is always built in global mode here. Only create reads it.

body.name: shared_test_cases
body.description: Cases shared in from other projects, as [{project_id, test_case_ids: [...]}]. Only this PATCH resolves them; the POST on the same path accepts the key and silently ignores it.

body.name: is_automation
body.description: Only honoured on this PATCH path (and only for the literal values true/false); the POST on the same path ignores it.

capabilities.intent: Change just the fields you name on a test run — rename it, move its state on, link or unlink a test plan, attach configurations or a dynamic filter — leaving everything you omit untouched
guidance: Two different operations share this path. This PATCH applies only the keys present in `test_run`; the POST rebuilds the whole payload and resets what you omit. This is the safe default for a targeted edit.
Unlinking is explicit: send test_plan_id (or sub_test_plan_id) as null or "" to detach the plan. Omitting the key keeps the current link.
run_state is validated here: an unknown value returns 400 echoing it. Both 'new_run' and 'new' are accepted. Omit the key to leave the state alone.

is_dynamic lives inside filter_test_cases and nowhere else. true needs at least one other criterion in the same object or the call 400s; false flips a dynamic run back to static; omitting it leaves the flag as it is.

Composition keys interact: sending only configurations re-reads the run's existing case selection so the case list survives, and sending selection keys without configurations re-reads the existing configuration list. Send neither and the run's composition is left completely untouched.
Cases are unioned in, never out — this cannot remove a case from the run. Removal is the bulk test-cases call, and that one drops the removed cases' results.
The body must be wrapped in a `test_run` object; without it the request 400s before any field is read.
There is no undo: test runs keep no version history, so an overwritten name, description or tag list cannot be restored.
The updated run comes back at the top level as `testrun` — one word, no underscore, and no `data` envelope. This differs from the read endpoints, which use `test_run`.

capabilities.name: update_test_case_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Test case IDENTIFIER, normally TC-NNN. The segment carries no route constraint, but the action resolves it through an identifier lookup scoped to this project, so only an identifier resolves: TC-NNN, or the case's third-party identifier in workspaces that issue project-level ids. The internal integer id the v1 test-case endpoints take does NOT resolve here and comes back 404 'Test case not found'.

body.name: name
body.description: Case title. Omit to leave it alone; sending an empty or whitespace-only string is rejected 422 'Test case name cannot be empty' rather than clearing it. Note the response calls this field `title`, not `name`.

body.name: description
body.description: Rich-text field. Links are stripped server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: preconditions
body.description: Rich-text field, same server-side link stripping as description.

body.name: test_case_folder_id
body.description: Move the case to this folder as part of the edit. This is the name the parameter filter accepts — `folder_id`, the name the response and the published schema use, is DROPPED here and the case silently stays put. Unlike the v1 edit path, a value equal to the current folder is not stripped before the write.

body.name: priority
body.description: The project's display value for priority (e.g. 'Low', 'Medium', 'High') or that value's numeric field id. Matched on the display value first, then on the id; anything else fails the WHOLE call with 400 'Invalid default field value priority'. Resolve the allowed set from the project's system field values first — it is per project, not a fixed list.

body.name: status
body.description: The project's display value for test-case status, or its numeric field id. Same matching and same 400 'Invalid default field value status' as priority. Not the run/result status — this is the case's own lifecycle field.

body.name: case_type
body.description: The project's display value for case type, or its numeric field id. Stored internally as the category, and a wrong value fails the whole call with 400 'Invalid default field value case_type'.

body.name: automation_status
body.description: Internal name, not a display label. Validated against this closed list before the request leaves the API with 400 'Invalid automation status', and then matched against the project's own automation-state options.

body.name: owner
body.description: Owner as an email address, or a TM user id. DANGER: an address that does not resolve to a user in this group is NOT an error — it is written as null, clearing the owner, and the call still returns 200. Verify the user before sending.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag-name strings. The list you send REPLACES the case's tags, so read the current tags and send the union if you mean to add one; `[]` clears them all; omit the key to leave them untouched.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked issue/defect ids as plain STRINGS on this path — the parameter filter here permits only scalars, so the {issue_id, issue_type} objects the v1 edit body takes are dropped and the links never happen. The list replaces the case's linked issues.

body.name: custom_fields
body.description: Keyed by the custom field's NAME here — not by its numeric id, which is what the v1 edit and bulk paths use. A key the project does not define is skipped SILENTLY and the call still returns 200; a defined field with an unusable value fails the whole call with 400 'Custom field validation failed for <name>'. Dropdown values are the option label; a user-type field takes an email.

body.name: test_case_steps
body.description: The case's ordered step list. `order` is overwritten by array position, so the array order is what counts. Omit the key to keep the existing steps. Rejected with 422 for a BDD-template case — send feature/background/scenario instead. This is the only surface that writes steps: the bulk edit refuses them outright.

body.name: template
body.description: Template NAME, not an id. Omit it and the case's current template is kept — the action fills it in from the stored case before the write.

body.name: template_id
body.description: Custom-template id. Must be a TestCase-entity template visible to the caller's group; an unknown or cross-group id is rejected 400 rather than quietly falling back to the system default. Explicit null is a no-op, not a clear.

body.name: feature
body.description: BDD-template cases only; 422 on a non-BDD case. Omit to keep the stored value — sending an EMPTY string is rejected 400 'Cannot clear feature and scenario for BDD test cases.'

body.name: background
body.description: BDD-template cases only; 422 on a non-BDD case. Omitted or blank keeps the stored background.

body.name: scenario
body.description: BDD-template cases only; 422 on a non-BDD case. Like feature, an empty string is rejected 400 rather than clearing it.

body.name: reviewers
body.description: Reviewer EMAILS. An array replaces the whole reviewer set ([] unassigns everyone). An object form {value: [...], operation: replace|add|remove} is also accepted for an additive or subtractive change. A bare string or null is dropped by the parameter filter and can never become a reviewer write. Revoked reviewers are emailed. Naming the case owner is rejected 422.

body.name: send_for_review
body.description: Moves the case into review and mails the reviewers, independently of `reviewers`. String booleans ('true'/'false'/'1'/'0'/'on'/'off') are cast; an ambiguous string such as 'yes' is rejected 422 rather than guessed.

body.name: review_status
body.description: Assignment states only — a verdict (approved / rejected / changes_requested) is one reviewer's decision and is rejected 422. OMIT this on a metadata-only edit: sending `pending` on an approved case invalidates the approval and writes an audit row. The pending/in_review narrowing only applies once the reviewer feature flag is on; with it off the value is passed through unvalidated.

body.name: identifier
body.description: Rewrites the case's THIRD-PARTY identifier, and only in workspaces configured to issue project-level ids; elsewhere it is ignored. A value already used in the project fails the call. This does not change the TC-NNN identifier.

body.name: expected_result
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT WRITTEN on this path — the parameter filter permits it and the request builder never copies it, so it is dropped before the write and you still get 200. The v1 edit paths do persist it. Never report an expected result as saved from here.

body.name: estimate
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NOT WRITTEN — passes validation and is then dropped before the write, exactly as on the v1 create/edit paths. Never report an estimate as saved.

body.name: is_shared
body.description: TRAP: sending this can only hurt you here. If the project has test-case sharing disabled the request is rejected 400 before anything is read; if it is enabled the field is dropped by this action's parameter filter and the sharing flag is unchanged — a 200 that did nothing. Use the sharing/bulk surface to share a case.

body.name: test_case_dataset
body.description: ACCEPTED BUT NEVER APPLIED on this path: the builder only regenerates dataset mappings when the modified-dataset flag is set, and that flag is not accepted by this action, so the existing mappings are always kept. Returns 200 with the dataset unchanged.

capabilities.intent: Change one existing test case — rename it, rewrite its steps, preconditions or description, set priority/status/type/owner, retag it, relink issues or put it into review — sending only the fields you want changed
guidance: This is the SINGLE-case update, addressed by one identifier. The bulk edits take a selection (ids or a filter) instead, refuse step lists, and key custom fields by numeric id — so when you are changing one case, and always when you are changing its steps, this is the one to use.

Both ids in the path are prefixed strings (PR-1 / TC-42). The case id is resolved by an identifier lookup inside the project, so the internal integer id that the v1 edit endpoints take returns 404 'Test case not found' here.

The body must be wrapped in a `test_case` object AND that object must be non-empty: a missing, null or empty wrapper is rejected 400 'Invalid request format: test_case parameter is missing or malformed' before any field is read.
Only the keys you send are written — omitted fields keep their stored values. There is no undo, but the case keeps version history, so a bad edit can be recovered by restoring the previous version.

Accepted and then silently discarded on this path, each returning 200: expected_result, estimate, is_shared, the dataset payload, and `folder_id` (use test_case_folder_id to move). Re-read the case before telling anyone these landed.

priority, status and case_type take the PROJECT's display value or that value's numeric id; one bad value fails the whole call with 400 'Invalid default field value <field>'. Resolve the allowed values from the project's system field values first rather than guessing 'P1' or 'Open'.
custom_fields is keyed by field NAME here (the v1 paths key by numeric id). An unknown name is skipped without error, so a typo means a 200 that changed nothing — confirm by reading the case back.
An owner that does not resolve to a user in this group is written as null and CLEARS the owner instead of erroring.
BDD and step-based cases are mutually exclusive: steps on a BDD case are 422, feature/background/scenario on a non-BDD case are 422, and clearing feature or scenario to an empty string is 400.

reviewers, send_for_review and review_status run a gate ladder (Team-Pro plan, the project's Review & Approve setting, 21 CFR Part 11) and are applied AFTER the case update has committed. A 502 with error_code reviewer_write_failed and test_case_updated true means the edit landed but the reviewer change did not — retry with only the reviewer field, never with the whole body.
Changing anything here can move the case out of an approved review state, and reviewer removals send email immediately.

200.description: The updated test case, in the v2 public shape (title, not name; no integer id).

502.description: The test case WAS updated but the reviewer change could not be applied (error_code reviewer_write_failed, test_case_updated true). Also returned with error_code review_approve_unknown, in which case nothing was written at all.

capabilities.name: move_test_case_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API. It is also the only project involved — the move cannot leave it.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Test case IDENTIFIER, normally TC-NNN. The segment carries no route constraint, but the action resolves it through an identifier lookup scoped to this project, so only an identifier resolves: TC-NNN, or the case's third-party identifier in workspaces that issue project-level ids. The internal integer id returns 404 'Test case not found'.

body.name: destination_folder_id
body.description: Target folder, as a plain positive INTEGER folder id — folders are not identified by a prefixed string. Sent at the TOP LEVEL of the body, not inside a `test_case` object (the bulk move is the opposite and nests it). Missing, non-numeric, zero or negative is refused before anything is read. A numeric string is accepted and coerced.

capabilities.intent: File one test case in a different folder — use this to reorganise the tree, move a case out of an inbox/triage folder, or put a case where a run or plan expects to find it
guidance: Within ONE project only: there is no destination-project field, and the case is looked up in the same project it is moved inside. A cross-project move is not available here.

One case per call. To move many, use the bulk move, which takes a selection under a `test_case` object and runs asynchronously past ~30 cases; this one is always synchronous and is the cleaner choice for a single case.

The destination is a plain integer folder id and is NOT guessable — resolve it from the project's folder tree first. Nothing in this layer checks that the folder belongs to this project, so a stray id from another project is only caught (or not) downstream.

Moving a case into the folder it is already in is accepted and returns 200 with the case unchanged. Unlike the v1 edit path, the same-folder value is not stripped before the write, so the upstream write still happens.
Capture the case's current folder before you call if you may want to undo: the response reports only the NEW folder, and moving back means calling this again with the old id.
Nothing but the folder changes — the identifier, steps, tags, owner and review state are untouched — and the response carries the whole case in the v2 public shape.

The same folder change can be made as part of a single-case update by sending test_case_folder_id in its body; use this endpoint when the move is all you want, because it needs no other field and cannot accidentally rewrite one.

200.description: The moved test case in the v2 public shape, with folder_id now the destination, plus a top-level message 'Test case moved successfully'.

capabilities.name: get_test_case_histories_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: Test case identifier: TC-NNN, or the third-party identifier set on the case. The route deliberately leaves this segment unconstrained, but it is resolved through identifier lookup before anything is read — a bare internal numeric case id is not a match and comes back 404 'Test case not found'.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read — you silently get page 1 again. Page size is fixed at 30 and is not caller-controllable here: `per_page` and `page_size` are accepted by the URL but ignored. A `p` that is not a positive integer (blank, zero, negative, non-numeric, repeated) is refused with 400 'Invalid Params'.

capabilities.intent: See what changed on a test case, when, and who changed it — the revision trail, newest first, naming the fields touched in each edit; the read to answer 'what did this case look like before that edit?' or 'which revision should we roll back to?'
guidance: Rows come newest first. Each row's `version_name` is a positional label — V1 is the oldest revision still visible, and the highest number is the newest edit on page 1.

`version_name` is the only handle a row gives you: the v2 rows carry no history record id. Strip the leading V and pass the number as the version number to the single-version read to pull that revision's full test case snapshot.

Only the newest row on each page is enriched with the per-field old/new `modified` map — the rest carry `modified_fields` (the field names only), so a per-field before/after for an older edit needs the single-version read for that version.

Without an Enterprise or Team Pro plan the caller sees only the last 30 days of history. Older revisions are simply absent and nothing in the response flags that the window was applied, so a short list is not proof that the case was rarely edited. Version numbers count only what is visible, so they renumber as old revisions age out.
Listing degrades gracefully across plans, but comparing two versions and restoring one are paid-plan only — fall back to listing plus single-version reads when those are refused.

Each record carries `source` ('create' on the first revision, 'update' for an edit, 'restore' after a rollback), `created_at`, `modified_fields`, and `updated_by` — the editor's email, null when that user cannot be resolved in this group. The raw `user_id` is the BrowserStack user id, not a Test Management one.
Page with `p`; the page size is fixed at 30, so a long-lived test case is walked 30 revisions at a time and the total is in `info.count`.

capabilities.name: list_test_runs_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again. 0 is treated as 1.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Rows per page, and NOT a free range: only the literal values 30 and 300 are accepted. Anything else (50, 100, 301) is refused with a 400 'parameter_error' rather than clamped, so ask for 300 directly when you want a large project in few calls.

query.name: include_closed
query.description: Include closed runs. Closed runs are EXCLUDED from this listing by default, so counts and 'all runs' answers are silently short without this. Pass the literal string 'true'.

query.name: run_state
query.description: Filter by lifecycle state. Supplying it also lifts the default closed-run exclusion on its own, so run_state=closed works without include_closed.

query.name: assignee
query.description: Comma-separated owner emails, resolved against this group. This filter FAILS OPEN: an address that matches no user in the group is silently dropped from the filter instead of erroring, so a typo widens the result set and still returns 200. Verify the emails resolve before trusting a filtered count.

query.name: test_plan_id
query.description: Restrict to runs linked to this test plan. An identifier that matches no plan in the project is a 404 ('Test Plan ID is invalid'), not an empty list.

query.name: created_after
query.description: Lower bound on creation date, YYYY-MM-DD. May be sent on its own. A value in a different format is a 400; a date later than tomorrow is a 400.

query.name: created_before
query.description: Upper bound on creation date, YYYY-MM-DD. May be sent on its own. Sending a created_after later than this is a 400 naming the start date.

query.name: closed_after
query.description: Lower bound on close date, YYYY-MM-DD. Sending either closed bound also forces the result to CLOSED runs only, whatever include_closed says.

query.name: closed_before
query.description: Upper bound on close date, YYYY-MM-DD. Sending either closed bound also forces the result to CLOSED runs only, whatever include_closed says.

capabilities.intent: Find test runs in a project — filter by owner, lifecycle state, linked plan or date to locate a run, count how many there are, or collect the run ids you need before linking runs to a test plan
guidance: Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `page_size`. page_size is an allow-list of exactly 30 and 300 — any other number is a 400 'parameter_error', not a clamp — so pass 300 when you want the project in as few calls as possible.

Closed runs are excluded by default. Without include_closed=true (or a run_state filter, which lifts the exclusion by itself) a 'how many runs do we have?' answer quietly omits every closed run and still comes back 200.

Rows carry the run's `identifier` (TR-14) and nothing numeric — this listing's serializer emits no `id` and no `uuid` field at all. TR-NNN is exactly what the newer single-run and run-test-case capabilities want in their paths, so for reading a run onward this is all you need.

Linking runs to a test plan is the exception: a plan's linked-run array takes the INTEGER run id. The TR-NNN string reaches the backing service uncoerced and 502s there, and this listing does not give you the integer. Resolve it first — the v1 project run listing (get_test_runs_v1) carries the integer as `uuid` on each run — and send that, never the TR-NNN string.

The assignee filter fails open while the plan and date filters fail closed: an unresolvable email is dropped silently, but an unknown TP-NNN is a 404 and a malformed or out-of-order date is a 400. Only the assignee filter can quietly widen your result.
closed_after / closed_before are not just a date window — either one restricts the whole result to closed runs.

Deep paging is capped by rows, not pages: once p x page_size passes roughly 30,000 the call returns 429 with error_code 'request_limit_exceeded'. Narrow with a filter rather than walking a large project to the end.
Rows are run headers only — progress is aggregated counts. To see which cases are in a run, read that run's test cases.

429.description: Deep-paging guard. Returned when page x page_size exceeds the account's row ceiling (30,000 by default).

message.example: Page count exceeds limit. Requests with more than 1000 pages are temporarily disabled. Please reduce the page count and try again.

capabilities.name: create_test_run_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

body.name: name
body.description: Run name. Optional in practice despite the published schema marking it required: omitting it names the run 'Test Run DD/MM/YYYY' from today's date rather than failing.

body.name: description
body.description: HTML is unescaped, sanitised and re-escaped server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: assignee
body.description: Run owner, as an email resolved inside this group. Unlike the run edit paths, an address that does not resolve is NOT an error here — it is dropped and the run is created owned by the calling user, so a typo produces a wrongly-owned run with a 200.

body.name: run_state
body.description: Lifecycle state, checked against this fixed list before any case selection is built. On create an absent or unrecognised value is not rejected — it is silently stored as new_run — so send the state you want explicitly rather than relying on a validation error.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings.

body.name: configurations
body.description: Configuration IDs (integers) the run executes against — not the configuration objects returned on read, and not the display names the published schema's example shows. Duplicates are collapsed. Overwritten entirely when configuration_map is also sent.

body.name: issues
body.description: Linked defects. Each entry is an object; a bare string entry is coerced to {issue_id: ...} but loses the tracker type.

body.name: test_plan_id
body.description: Parent test plan to link at creation. Resolved by identifier — a TP-NNN that matches no plan in this project fails the whole create with 404, the run is not created. Mutually exclusive with sub_test_plan_id; when both are sent test_plan_id wins.

body.name: sub_test_plan_id
body.description: Sub test plan to link at creation. Mutually exclusive with test_plan_id.

body.name: test_cases
body.description: Test case identifiers to put in the run. This, shared_test_cases, folder_ids and include_all are the ONLY inputs that actually place cases in a run — filter_test_cases alone does not.

body.name: shared_test_cases
body.description: Cases shared in from other projects: a list of {project_id, test_case_ids: [...]} objects. The flat/scalar form is stripped by the parameter filter and silently yields zero mapped cases, so always send the object shape. Not present in the published schema.

body.name: include_all
body.description: Put every test case in the project into the run.

body.name: folder_ids
body.description: Folder IDs (integers) whose cases go into the run.

body.name: include_sub_folders
body.description: Descend into sub-folders of folder_ids. Sending this key with folder_ids absent or empty is a hard 400 ('Cannot process nested folders of empty folder array'), so only send it alongside a non-empty folder_ids.

body.name: filter_test_cases
body.description: Forward-matching rule for the run, and the only place is_dynamic is read. Sending it ALONE does not select cases: the run is created empty and marked dynamic. Labels ('High', 'Draft') are resolved to ids; an owner email that does not resolve in this group fails the create with 400. is_dynamic:true needs at least one other key here or it is a 400.

body.name: filter_scope
body.description: How filter_test_cases combines with folder_ids: 'global' unions them across the project, 'within_folders' intersects the filter with the listed folders. Honoured on create only — the run update paths accept it and ignore it.

body.name: configuration_map
body.description: Per-case configuration assignment: each entry is {test_case_id: "TC-1" or ["TC-1","TC-2"], configuration_ids: [101,102]}. Sending it REPLACES the top-level configurations list with the ids used here. It is an overlay, not the case list — cases selected elsewhere still come in, with a null-configuration row.

body.name: test_case_assignee
body.description: Default assignee applied to the cases placed in the run, as an email. Applied by the asynchronous population step, not at create time. Not present in the published schema.

body.name: is_automation
body.description: Accepted and then DROPPED — it does not make the run an automation run. It is still read to decide which write permission is demanded, so sending true can 403 a caller who could have created a manual run. Leave it out unless you mean to request the automation permission.

capabilities.intent: Create a test run in a project and load it with the test cases to be executed — the starting point for recording results, and what you make before assigning testers or linking the run to a plan
guidance: Every field goes inside a `test_run` object. A flat body is rejected before a single field is read.

Only test_cases, shared_test_cases, folder_ids or include_all actually put cases in the run. filter_test_cases is a forward-sync rule, NOT a selection: a create carrying only filter_test_cases returns 200 with an EMPTY run and silently marks it dynamic even though you did not ask. If the user named cases, list them.

Create runs STATIC unless the user explicitly asked for one that keeps picking up new cases. A dynamic run matches on nine fields only — priority, status, category, owner, automation_status, automation_state, folder, tags, issues — so a 'cases created in the last 7 days' filter is stored, echoed back on read, and never matched, and the run over-collects forever.

is_dynamic belongs inside filter_test_cases and nowhere else; a top-level is_dynamic is stripped by the parameter filter and has no effect. is_dynamic:true with no other key inside filter_test_cases is a 400 saying filter criteria are required.

A bare 400 'invalid data' is about the run's own fields — it is raised while converting the run header, before any case selection is built — most often an owner or reviewer inside filter_test_cases that resolves to no user in this group. It is never a complaint about the shape of your selection.

Populating the run is asynchronous. A 200 means the run exists, not that its cases are attached yet; re-read the run's test cases to confirm. A 202 with build_pending:true means the run was created but is not readable back yet — poll for it, never retry the create, which would make a second run.
include_sub_folders is only meaningful next to a non-empty folder_ids; on its own it is a hard 400.

A run created here keeps no version history. If the wrong cases land in it, adding is easy but removing is a separate operation, and the run's own metadata cannot be rolled back — only overwritten or the run deleted.
The new run comes back at the top level as `test_run`, not under `data` — unlike the v1 create, which wraps its payload in `data`.

202.description: The run was created but is not yet readable back — its build is still being provisioned and case population is in progress. Poll for the run rather than retrying the create.

message.example: Test run was created; its build is still being created and population is in progress.

capabilities.name: list_test_plans_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again.

query.name: count
query.description: Rows per page; read first when both this and page_size are sent. Defaults to 30. Above 300 the call is refused with 400 'Page limit exceeds the maximum limit of 300' rather than clamped.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Alias for count, read only when count is absent. Same 300 ceiling and the same 400 above it.

capabilities.intent: List the test plans in a project — the read that turns a plan name the user said into the TP-NNN id every other plan call needs, and answers 'what plans do we have?'
guidance: Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and size with `count` (or `page_size`). Default 30, hard ceiling 300 — asking for more errors instead of clamping, so ask for 300 in one go rather than walking 30 at a time.
Deep paging is capped on rows, not pages: once p x page_size passes the account's limit (30,000 by default) the call returns 429 'request_limit_exceeded'.

There is NO filtering on this route — no name search, status, owner, tag or sort parameter is read here. Page through and match client-side, or use the v1 plan listing, which does take status/sort/include_sub_plans.

Whether sub-plans (STP-NNN) appear among these rows is decided by the backing service and is not steerable from here. Read each row's parent_plan_id rather than assuming, and list a parent's children through the sub-plans listing.

Rows are the same plan shape the single-plan read returns, minus the embedded runs. Carry `identifier` (TP-NNN / STP-NNN) forward — it is what the v2 plan paths take, not the numeric id the v1 plan capabilities use.
Page against the `info` envelope (page, page_size, count, next, prev) instead of probing for an empty page.

capabilities.name: create_test_plan_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

body.name: name
body.description: Plan name, and the only required field. Blank or missing fails the whole call with 400 'Name field cannot be blank' before anything is created.

body.name: description
body.description: Rich text. Sanitised server-side against the HTML allowlist and links are rewritten, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: start_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD); stored as midnight UTC. An unparseable value is dropped silently rather than refused.

body.name: end_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD). Earlier than start_date fails the call with 400 'Please check date params'.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings. A non-string entry makes the whole list fall back to empty — no error, just an untagged plan.

body.name: issues
body.description: Plain issue keys, not objects: the v1 structured {issue_id, issue_type, metadata} form is filtered out here. Each key is stored as a jira-type link unless issue_tracker says otherwise. Linking is queued asynchronously, so the issues may not yet appear on an immediate re-read.

body.name: issue_tracker
body.description: Resolves the keys in `issues` against a connected tracker, adding ticket metadata. Needs BOTH name ('jira') and host; a host that matches no JIRA site connected to the caller's account fails the call with 'Invalid issue tracker'. Omit it and issues are stored as bare jira references.

body.name: created_at
body.description: Backdated creation time, for migrating plans in from another tool. Sits at the TOP level of the body, not inside test_plan, and is only honoured for groups with the external-API timestamp feature enabled — otherwise it is ignored silently. Unparseable is 400.

body.name: updated_at
body.description: Backdated last-update time. Top level like created_at, same feature gate. Must be >= created_at (or >= now when created_at is absent), else 400.

capabilities.intent: Create a test plan to group the test runs for a release, sprint or milestone — the TP-NNN it returns is what runs and sub-plans then hang off
guidance: Wrap the fields in a `test_plan` object. An unwrapped flat body also works, but a body wrapped under any other key (`plan`, `sub_test_plan`) is read as empty and fails with 400 'Name field cannot be blank'.
The plan is always created in the `new` state: a plan_status in the create body is not read at all. Move it to started/completed afterwards with the update capability.
Owner is always the calling user — there is no owner field on this route, unlike the v1 create.
This route always creates a TOP-LEVEL plan; parent_plan_id is not read. To create a child, use the sub-plan create under its parent — parentage cannot be changed afterwards on v2.
Reviewers, attachments and custom fields are v1-only on plans; sending them here changes nothing and is not reported.
Recoverable: a plan created by mistake can be archived or deleted afterwards, so nothing here is one-way.
The response is the created plan under `test_plan`; take `identifier` (TP-NNN) from it — the numeric id the v1 plan capabilities need is not in this payload.

capabilities.name: get_test_plan_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_plan_id
path_params.description: Plan identifier in TP-NNN form, or STP-NNN for a sub-plan — both match this route. The integer plan id the v1 plan capabilities take does NOT match here and gives a routing 404.

capabilities.intent: Read one test plan or sub-plan — dates, status, owner-facing description, tags, linked issues, how many runs and sub-plans it holds, and a first glimpse of the runs inside it
guidance: Pass an STP-NNN to read a sub-plan: the same route serves both, and the plan still comes back under the `test_plan` key (never `sub_test_plan`).

The embedded `test_runs` array is a preview, not the membership list: only identifier and name, and only the first 30 runs of the plan. Use the plan's test-runs read to page through them or to see run state and progress.

If the upstream run fetch fails, the call still returns 200 with the `test_runs` and `links` keys ABSENT. Absent is not the same as an empty plan — check test_runs_count before concluding a plan has no runs.
test_runs_count splits active/closed and counts this plan's own runs only. sub_plans_count is populated on a top-level plan; parent_plan_id is set only on a sub-plan and carries the parent's TP-NNN.
active_state is derived: 'completed' once the plan is completed, otherwise 'active'. It does not distinguish a new plan from a started one.
A wrong, mistyped or other-project id is a 404 'Test Plan ID is invalid. Please enter valid Test plan ID and try again' — the same message for every not-found case.
Whether an archived plan is readable here is not settled by this route; treat a 404 on a plan the user insists exists as a possible archive and check the archived listing.

capabilities.name: create_sub_test_plan_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_plan_id
path_params.description: The PARENT plan, as TP-NNN. This is where the new child hangs; it is not the id of the plan being created. An unknown parent is a 404 before anything is created.

body.name: name
body.description: Sub-plan name, and the only required field. Blank or missing fails the call with 400 'Name field cannot be blank'.

body.name: description
body.description: Rich text. Sanitised server-side against the HTML allowlist and links are rewritten, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: start_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD); stored as midnight UTC. Not validated against the parent plan's dates — a child may sit entirely outside its parent's window.

body.name: end_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD). Earlier than start_date fails the call with 400 'Please check date params'.

body.name: tags
body.description: Plain tag strings. Tags are not inherited from the parent plan. A non-string entry makes the whole list fall back to empty, with no error.

body.name: issues
body.description: Plain issue keys, not objects. Stored as jira-type links unless issue_tracker says otherwise, and queued asynchronously so they may lag an immediate re-read.

body.name: issue_tracker
body.description: Resolves the keys in `issues` against a connected tracker. Needs BOTH name ('jira') and host; a host matching no JIRA site connected to the caller's account fails the call with 'Invalid issue tracker'.

capabilities.intent: Break a test plan into a child plan — use this when a release plan needs per-team, per-phase or per-platform slices that each hold their own runs
guidance: Wrap the body in a `sub_test_plan` object, NOT `test_plan`: only that key is read on this route, so a test_plan-wrapped body is seen as empty and 400s with 'Name field cannot be blank' however complete it was.
The parent comes from the path; there is no parent_plan_id field, and a sub-plan cannot be re-parented or promoted afterwards on v2.

The created plan comes back under `sub_test_plan` (not test_plan) and its identifier is STP-NNN. That STP id is accepted wherever a plan id is taken on these v2 plan routes — read it, edit it, list its runs.
Runs are not moved here: a new sub-plan starts empty, and a run is attached by setting its plan on the run itself, which unlinks it from whichever plan held it before.
Recoverable: an unwanted sub-plan can be deleted or archived afterwards.
Completed sub-plans are hidden from the sub-plan listing, so a child you create and later complete stops appearing there even though it still exists.

capabilities.name: get_test_plan_test_runs_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_plan_id
path_params.description: Plan identifier in TP-NNN form, or STP-NNN to list a sub-plan's own runs. The integer plan id the v1 capabilities take does not match this route.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again. This is the ONLY paging control here — the page size is fixed.

capabilities.intent: List the test runs that belong to a test plan, with each run's state, assignee and pass/fail progress — the read behind 'how is this release going?' and 'which runs are in this plan?'
guidance: Page with `p` only. The page size is FIXED at 30 and cannot be raised: `count` and `page_size` are documented on this route but not read, so asking for 100 still returns 30. Page against the `info` envelope.
Rows carry `identifier` (TR-NNN) but NO numeric run id — the integer uuid some plan-linking calls need is not in this payload, so read the run itself when you need it.
There is no include-sub-plan-runs switch here (v1 has one). To cover a parent and its children, list each sub-plan's runs separately.

When the upstream run service fails, the body STILL says success: true with test_runs null while the HTTP status carries the real failure. Check that test_runs is an array before reading 'no runs' as an empty plan.
Progress arrives as overall_progress, a map of status name to count for the run's cases; a run with nothing executed may omit the key entirely rather than report zeros.
This lists runs, not results or cases — drill into a run's test cases for case-level state.

capabilities.name: update_test_plan_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: test_plan_id
path_params.description: Plan to edit, as TP-NNN — or STP-NNN to edit a sub-plan through this same route. The integer plan id the v1 capabilities take does not match here.

body.name: name
body.description: New name. Optional here, unlike the v1 plan edit which rejects any body without it. An empty string is ignored and the current name is kept — the name cannot be cleared.

body.name: description
body.description: New description. An empty string is ignored and the stored description is kept, so a description cannot be cleared here. Sanitised server-side, so the stored value can differ from what you sent.

body.name: start_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD). Applied only when non-empty; omitted leaves the current date. Once the plan is started this is fixed and further values for it are ignored.

body.name: end_date
body.description: Plain date (YYYY-MM-DD). Applied only when non-empty. Earlier than the plan's start date is refused with 400 'Invalid end_date, should be greater than start_date' and nothing is saved.

body.name: plan_status
body.description: Lifecycle move. Only forward, one step at a time: new -> started -> completed. 'started' stamps start_date (today unless you send one) and 'completed' stamps end_date the same way.

body.name: tags
body.description: REPLACES the plan's tags with this list. An empty array is treated as 'not sent' and leaves the existing tags in place, so tags cannot be cleared through this call.

body.name: issues
body.description: Plain issue keys, not the v1 structured objects. Sent non-empty they replace the linked set; an empty array is ignored, so links cannot be removed here. Processing is queued, so an immediate re-read may lag.

body.name: issue_tracker
body.description: Resolves the keys in `issues` against a connected tracker. Needs BOTH name ('jira') and host; a host matching no JIRA site connected to the caller's account fails the call with 'Invalid issue tracker'.

capabilities.intent: Change an existing test plan or sub-plan — rename it, move its dates, retag it, relink issues, or start/complete it; note that attaching or detaching a test run is NOT done from the plan on v2, it is set on the run
guidance: Merge, not replace: only the fields you send change and anything omitted keeps its current value, so a one-field edit is safe. (The v2 run 'update' on the same path shape behaves the opposite way — do not carry that habit here.)

Linking runs is the trap. A `test_runs` list in this body is SILENTLY DISCARDED — 200, plan unchanged, nothing linked, no warning. It is a v1-only field. On v2 you set the run's plan from the run side (its test_plan_id / sub_test_plan_id), and that MOVES the run: a run belongs to at most one plan, so the plan that held it loses it with nothing in the response to say so. Check the runs' current plans first and tell the user which plans will lose runs.
Unlike the v1 plan edit, name is NOT required — an update carrying only dates, tags or a status move is accepted.

Lifecycle is one-way and one step at a time: new -> completed is 400 'Cannot directly complete test plan', started -> new is 400 'Cannot revert started test plan', and once completed the plan is FROZEN — every later edit, including a rename, is 400 'Cannot update completed test plan'. Complete a plan last.
No undo: plans keep no version history, so a name, description or date this call overwrites cannot be restored and there is nothing to roll back to. Read the plan first if the old value matters.
Clearing is not possible through this call: empty strings and empty arrays are read as 'not sent' for name, description, tags and issues.

Wrap the body in a `test_plan` object even when the target is a sub-plan (STP-NNN) on this route — `sub_test_plan` is not read here, and the reply also comes back under `test_plan`. An unwrapped flat body is accepted too.
Owner, reviewers, attachments, custom fields and re-parenting are v1-only on plans; sending them here changes nothing and is not reported.
A rejected edit returns 400 with {success: false, error: ...} and saves nothing — the plan is left exactly as it was.

capabilities.name: list_custom_fields_v2

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page` is not read on this listing: send it and you silently get page 1 again. A zero, negative, non-numeric or repeated value is refused with 400 'Invalid Params' rather than coerced.

query.name: count
query.description: Rows per page. Defaults to 30 and the real ceiling is 300 — a larger value is REFUSED with 400 'Page limit exceeds the maximum limit of 300', not clamped, so ask for 300 directly on a large workspace. The published spec claims a maximum of 100; the code enforces 300.

capabilities.intent: Discover the test-case custom fields defined in this workspace — list each field with its name, type, required flag and linked-project count, and pick up the numeric field id needed before reading, editing or filling in a field
guidance: Page with `p` and `count` — not `page` / `per_page`, which this listing ignores. `count` above 300 is a 400 naming the limit, so request 300 when you want the workspace in as few calls as possible.

Only TestCase fields are listed. The entity type is fixed server-side, so test-result, test-plan and exploratory-session fields never appear here whatever you send — the workspace field listing on the admin-settings surface is the one that covers those.

Rows are field metadata only: no dropdown options, no dataset and no list of linked projects, just a linked_projects_count. Read the field's datasets when you need the option values or the actual project links.

This is the newer public custom-fields surface. The admin-settings custom-field capabilities read the same stored definitions but answer in a different envelope and cover every entity type — prefer this one for test-case fields, and fall back to those for result/plan fields and for dataset or option editing.
Carry the numeric `id` from each row forward: that is exactly what the single-field read and the field edit take in their path.
Needs the field-view permission when role-based access is on. Without it the answer is 403 'This action is not permitted for the user', not an empty list.

capabilities.name: create_custom_field_v2

body.name: field_type
body.description: The kind of field. Mandatory in practice even though the body schema marks nothing required — anything outside this list is a flat 400 'Invalid Params'. It is fixed for the life of the field: the edit capability will not change it.

body.name: field_name
body.description: Label shown on the test case. Mandatory; trimmed before storage, so ' Priority' is stored as 'Priority'. Over 256 characters or blank is a 400 'Invalid Params'. Names that collide with a system field are refused separately (see guidance).

body.name: is_required
body.description: Whether a test case must fill this field. Mandatory, and it must be a real JSON boolean: the string "true" fails the parameter check with a flat 400 'Invalid Params' that names no field.

body.name: place_holder_text
body.description: Hint text shown in the empty field. Trimmed before storage; over 256 characters is a 400 'Invalid Params'.

body.name: default_value
body.description: Accepted by the schema but NOT settable here: for every non-boolean type it is discarded before the write, and for boolean the checks contradict each other (a JSON boolean fails the body schema, the string 'true' fails the parameter check). Set it afterwards with the field edit capability.

body.name: entity_type
body.description: What the field attaches to. Only TestCase exists on this route — any other value is 400 'Only TestCase entity type is supported'. Result, plan and exploratory-session fields are created on the admin-settings surface instead.

body.name: options
body.description: Choices for dropdown / multi_dropdown. Persisted ONLY when the request also carries applies_to_all_projects or assigned_projects — sent alone they are silently dropped while still being echoed in the response. For multi_dropdown every is_default is forced to false; for dropdown only the first is_default:true survives.

fields.name: option_value
fields.description: The choice as the user sees it. Must be non-empty.

fields.name: is_default
fields.description: Pre-selected choice. At most one per dropdown; ignored for multi_dropdown.

body.name: applies_to_all_projects
body.description: Link the new field to every project that exists today. Heavy: the server enumerates the whole workspace (stopping around 3000 projects) and links each one. NOTE this is not the same flag as on the edit capability, where it only toggles future-project linking.

body.name: assigned_projects
body.description: Projects that should offer this field, as PR-NNN identifiers — never numeric project ids. Every identifier is resolved first and one unknown entry fails the whole call with 400 'Not all project identifiers could be found'. The list echoed back in the response is truncated to the first 30.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: link_to_future_projects
body.description: Automatically offer this field in projects created later. Only meaningful alongside applies_to_all_projects or assigned_projects, because it is stored on the dataset those build.

body.name: levels
body.description: Hierarchy tiers, REQUIRED for field_type nested_dropdown and ignored for every other type. At least two entries, each with name and level_type; the schema refuses a nested_dropdown create without them.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Tier label, e.g. COUNTRY.

fields.name: level_type
fields.description: Widget for the tier, e.g. dropdown.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Position of the tier, top tier first.

body.name: parent_custom_field_id
body.description: For nested_dropdown the KEY must be present even when the value is null — the upstream nested-create path is chosen on the key's presence. Set to an existing nested field's id to add one more tier to it, in which case only field_name is validated and the rest is copied from the parent.

body.name: datasets
body.description: Advanced, forwarded upstream as sent. Lets one call define option values and project links together, including a recursive children tree for nested_dropdown. Prefer options + assigned_projects / applies_to_all_projects; reach for this only when you need nested option trees or explicit unlinks.

fields.name: linked_to_all_projects
fields.description: Expand to every project in the workspace before sending.

fields.name: linked_projects
fields.description: Numeric project ids to link on this dataset (this path takes ids, not PR-NNN identifiers).

fields.name: unlinked_projects
fields.description: Numeric project ids to unlink on this dataset.

fields.name: link_to_future_projects
fields.description: Link projects created later.

fields.name: options
fields.description: Option rows; each may carry a children array one tier down for nested_dropdown.

capabilities.intent: Define a new test-case custom field — choose its type, name it, say whether filling it is mandatory, and optionally give a dropdown its choices and link it to the projects that should offer it
guidance: field_type, field_name and is_required are all mandatory although the body schema marks nothing required, and is_required must be a real JSON boolean. Every failure of that validator comes back as the same 400 'Invalid Params' with no field named, so check all three before retrying.

options are only stored when the same request also carries applies_to_all_projects or assigned_projects — the choices live on a dataset, and no dataset is built without one of those. Sent alone they are dropped, and the response still echoes them, so a dropdown can look configured while holding no values. Re-read the field's datasets to confirm.

The returned custom_field is partly an echo of the request: options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects are replayed from what you sent (or defaulted to false / empty), not read back from storage. Only id, field_name, field_type, entity_type and is_required are authoritative.

assigned_projects takes PR-NNN identifiers, not numeric project ids, and one unresolvable identifier fails the whole create with 400 — resolve the projects first. applies_to_all_projects:true instead walks every project in the workspace (up to about 3000) and links them all, which is a slow call on a large account.
default_value cannot be set at create time for any type. Create the field, then set it through the field edit capability, where a boolean default is sent as the string 'true' or 'false'.

These names are reserved and rejected with 400 'Field with same name already exists. Use a unique name.': Title, Description, Preconditions, Steps, Result, Attachments, State, Owner, Priority, Type of Test Case, Automation Status, Tags, Jira Issues, Asana Issues, Review Status.
Choose the type carefully — it can never be edited. Changing a field's type in practice means deleting it and creating it again, which destroys every value already stored on test cases.

nested_dropdown needs levels with at least two entries (name + level_type each) and the parent_custom_field_id key present even when null. To append one more tier to an existing nested field, send parent_custom_field_id plus field_name and nothing else.

Same stored fields as the admin-settings create capability, different contract: this route is TestCase-only, takes PR-NNN project identifiers rather than numeric ids, and answers with a serialized custom_field object instead of the raw upstream record.
Needs the field-write permission; 403 otherwise. The new field can be removed again, but any values captured on test cases in the meantime go with it.

capabilities.name: get_custom_field_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The field's numeric id, as the custom-fields listing returns it. It is validated as a positive integer before anything else runs: a non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 'Invalid Params: id must be a positive integer'. The published spec showing a prefixed 'cf-123' string is wrong.

query.name: page
query.description: Page of the datasets fetched behind this field, reflected in dataset_ids / dataset_urls. `p` is accepted as a legacy alias for the same thing. Zero or non-numeric falls back to 1 instead of erroring.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Datasets per page behind this field. Defaults to 20 here (not 30) and is clamped at 300 rather than refused. Most fields have a single dataset, so this rarely matters.

capabilities.intent: Read one custom field by its numeric id — confirm its name, type, placeholder, default and whether it is mandatory, and pick up the ids of the datasets that hold its option values
guidance: applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects come back hardcoded false on this read. They are shape fillers, not the field's real project configuration — never report project scope from this response; read the field's datasets for that.
No option values are included. What you get is dataset_ids plus ready-made dataset_urls and datasets_url; follow one of those to see the choices a dropdown offers and which projects it is linked to.
An id that exists nowhere is 404 'Custom field not found', while an id that is not a positive integer is 400 — the two are distinguishable, so do not treat a 400 as 'no such field'.
The `project` query parameter documented in the spec is not read by this route. Filtering a field's option values by project is done on the dataset listing, not here.
Needs the field-view permission when role-based access is on; 403 otherwise.

Same stored definition as the admin-settings single-field read, but a different body: that one returns the field with its datasets and options inline, this one returns metadata plus dataset references.

capabilities.name: update_custom_field_v2

path_params.name: id
path_params.description: The field's numeric id. Validated as a positive integer before the field is loaded: a non-numeric or non-positive value is 400 'Invalid Params: id must be a positive integer', and an id with no field behind it is 404 'Custom field not found'.

body.name: field_name
body.description: New label. Omit it to keep the current one — this is a partial update. An empty string does NOT clear the name, it leaves the stored value untouched. Renaming onto a reserved system-field name is refused with 400.

body.name: is_required
body.description: Whether the field must be filled. Omit to keep the current setting; false is honoured (unlike the text attributes, this one is applied even when falsy). Must be a real JSON boolean.

body.name: place_holder_text
body.description: New hint text, trimmed before storage. Omit to keep the current one. An empty string does not clear it — the stored value survives.

body.name: default_value
body.description: New default. Unlike the create call this one is applied, for every field type. On a boolean field send the STRING "true" or "false" — it is coerced to "1"/"0", a real JSON boolean is rejected by the body schema, and an empty or falsy value leaves the stored default in place.

body.name: options
body.description: Replaces the dropdown's option list WHOLE on the field's existing dataset — options you leave out are removed and the values test cases hold for them are gone, in every linked project, with no undo. Send the full intended list. Ignored on non-dropdown field types.

fields.name: option_value
fields.description: The choice as the user sees it.

fields.name: is_default
fields.description: Pre-selected choice.

body.name: assigned_projects
body.description: The COMPLETE set of projects the field should apply to, as PR-NNN identifiers. It is diffed against the current links: anything currently linked and missing here is unlinked, which destroys the values stored in those projects. Use linked_projects / unlinked_projects for an incremental change.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: linked_projects
body.description: Projects to ADD, as PR-NNN identifiers. Sending this (or unlinked_projects) switches off the assigned_projects diff entirely, so existing links you do not mention are left alone. An identifier that resolves to no project fails the call with 400.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: unlinked_projects
body.description: Projects to REMOVE, as PR-NNN identifiers. Unlinking discards the values those projects' test cases hold for this field and cannot be undone. An unresolvable identifier fails the call with 400.

fields.name: identifier
fields.description: A project identifier such as PR-12345.

body.name: link_to_future_projects
body.description: Whether projects created later automatically offer this field. Applied to the field's dataset; sending it is itself enough to trigger the dataset write.

body.name: applies_to_all_projects
body.description: Legacy alias that here ONLY sets the future-projects flag — it does not link the projects that already exist, unlike the same flag at create time. An explicit link_to_future_projects wins over it. Use linked_projects to reach existing projects.

body.name: levels
body.description: Nested-dropdown tiers, forwarded upstream but currently ignored there for renames. Rename or retype a tier by editing that tier's own field id instead.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Existing tier field id.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Tier label.

fields.name: level_type
fields.description: Widget for the tier.

fields.name: index
fields.description: Position of the tier.

capabilities.intent: Change an existing test-case custom field — rename it, make it mandatory or optional, adjust its placeholder or default value, replace a dropdown's choices, or change which projects offer it
guidance: This is a PARTIAL update: every attribute you leave out keeps its stored value, so sending field_name alone is a valid rename. It differs from the admin-settings update capability, which is a full replace demanding field_name, field_type and is_required together.

None of it can be undone. Option lists and project links are rewritten in place, there is no bin and no prior revision: an option dropped from `options` is removed from the dataset and every value test cases hold for it disappears across all linked projects.

assigned_projects is read as the complete desired set, not an addition — any currently linked project you omit is unlinked, and the values stored there go with it. Count and name the projects you are about to drop before sending, or use linked_projects / unlinked_projects to change links one at a time.

field_type is not editable here. A field_type in the body is ignored, the stored type is kept and the call still answers 200, so never report a type change as done. A guard meant to refuse it with 400 exists but cannot fire, because the stored field is loaded after that check runs.

Empty strings do not clear anything: field_name, place_holder_text and default_value are applied only when non-empty, so the stored value survives an attempt to blank it. is_required is the exception — false is written.

Dataset-side changes (options, assigned_projects, linked_projects, unlinked_projects, link_to_future_projects, applies_to_all_projects) only take effect on dropdown, multi_dropdown and nested_dropdown fields. On any other type they are accepted, answered 200 and quietly ignored. If the field has no dataset yet, one is created.
applies_to_all_projects means something different here than at create time: it only toggles the future-projects flag and never links existing projects.

The two halves are not atomic. Field attributes are written first, the dataset second, so a failure on the dataset call leaves the rename or required-flag change already applied. Re-read the field before retrying.

The response replays options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects from your request rather than from storage — only the field attributes in it are read back. Confirm project links and option values by reading the field's datasets.
Needs the field-write permission; 403 otherwise. Unknown id is 404, a non-integer id is 400.

capabilities.name: list_reports_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again with a 200. Rows come back newest-created first.

query.name: page_size
query.description: Rows per page, and NOT a free range: only the literal values 30 and 300 are accepted. Anything else (5, 50, 100, 301) is refused with a 400 naming the two allowed values rather than clamped, so ask for 300 directly when you want a whole project in few calls.

query.name: is_scheduled
query.description: Narrows to recurring (scheduled) reports only, and it is a one-way switch: the filter is applied only when the value is exactly the string 'true'. is_scheduled=false applies NO filter and returns both kinds, so it cannot be used to find one-off reports — read the is_scheduled flag on each row for that.

query.name: report_type
query.description: Exact-match filter on the stored report type DISPLAY NAME, including spaces and capitals. A near-miss ('test run summary', 'Test Runs Summary') is not an error — it returns 200 with an empty list, which reads exactly like 'this project has no such reports'.

query.name: q[query]
query.description: Case-insensitive substring search across report title AND report type, matched together. The parameter is nested and must go on the wire as q[query]=term. A flat q=term is not an error and not a search: the filter is skipped and you get the full unfiltered list with a 200.

capabilities.intent: Find a project's reports — search saved and scheduled reports by title or type, see which ones run on a recurring schedule and when each next fires, or pick up the SC-NNN identifier of a report you then want to read or download
guidance: Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `page_size`. page_size is an allow-list of exactly 30 and 300 — any other number is a 400, not a clamp — so pass 300 when you want the project in as few calls as possible.
Both one-off and scheduled reports are listed by default; is_scheduled=true narrows to scheduled ones, and nothing narrows to one-off ones.

scheduled_report_count and total_report_count describe the WHOLE filtered result set, not the page you are holding — use them to answer 'how many?' without paging, but remember any report_type / q / is_scheduled filter you sent is already baked into both numbers.

Each row's `id` is the SC-NNN identifier, and that is what the v2 single-report read and the v2 download take. It is NOT the integer report id the v1 report capabilities (report detail, report sections, drilldown, send-email-now) require: SC-NNN is a per-group sequence number, so stripping the prefix gives the wrong id. Get the integer from the v1 schedules listing, which returns `id` and `identifier` side by side on the same records.
Rows carry the report's CONFIGURATION only — type, timeframe, filters, schedule, recipients. No figures, no report data. Reading the numbers a report contains is a separate call.

`latest_attachment` is derived from the newest generated file in the whole PROJECT, not from this report — a row can advertise an attachment produced by a different report. Treat it as 'something was generated here recently', not as this report's output.
`dynamic_filters` is always null on every row, even for reports created with dynamic filters; only `report_filters` echoes back what was configured.
Cross-project reports appear under every project they cover, so the same SC-NNN can show up in more than one project's listing.

capabilities.name: create_report_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project the report is filed under, in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all. For a multi-project report this project is still the owner; the full set goes in project_ids.

body.name: report_type
body.description: What the report reports on, as a DISPLAY NAME — the set is closed and matched exactly, spaces and capitals included. Anything else is a 400 'Validation error. Invalid report type'. Never substitute a neighbour: an activity question is 'Test Case Activity', not 'Test Run Summary'.

body.name: report_timeframe
body.description: What the report covers: either a rolling window, or a mode that says the scope comes from report_filters (specific_test_runs / specific_test_plans / specific_sessions / requirements). 'custom' pairs with custom_date_range. 'specific_test_cases' exists in the data model but is rejected here with a 400 'Specific test cases are not supported yet'.

body.name: report_creation_mode
body.description: Required — a create without it is a 400 'Invalid report creation mode', despite reading like an internal flag. Use custom_report for anything a caller is setting up; system_generated marks reports the product creates for itself.

body.name: title
body.description: Display name. NOT required despite the spec marking it so: omit it and the server fills in '<report_type>-MM/DD/YYYY' (today's date), which is easy to mistake later for a report someone else made. Titles are not unique, and this is the field the list search matches on.

body.name: description
body.description: Free-text note stored with the report. Not searched by the list endpoint's query filter, which looks only at title and report type.

body.name: custom_date_range
body.description: The window for report_timeframe='custom', as ONE string holding two YYYY-MM-DD dates separated by a space — not an array and not two fields. Read only when the timeframe is 'custom'; omitting it there is accepted silently and leaves the report with no window. A start after the end, or a start later than tomorrow, is a 400.

body.name: frequency
body.description: How often the report is generated and mailed. 'once' (or omitting this) means a one-off, unscheduled report. A recurring value only takes effect when frequency_details is sent with it — frequency alone is silently ignored and you get a one-off back with a 201.

body.name: frequency_details
body.description: The when for a recurring report. Must travel WITH frequency: send either both or neither. Ignored when frequency is 'once'.

fields.name: time
fields.description: 24-hour HH:MM. Anything else ('9am', '25:99', '5:00 PM') is a 400 'Invalid report frequency'.

fields.name: day
fields.description: Required for weekly as a lowercase English day name (monday…sunday), and for monthly as a day number 1-28. Unused for daily. 29-31 are rejected.

body.name: mail_to
body.description: Recipients of the generated report. Only used when the report is genuinely recurring — for a one-off it is accepted and then ignored entirely, so nobody is emailed.

fields.name: users
fields.description: EMAIL ADDRESSES (the v1 surface took integer user ids here). Every address must belong to a user in your group; one that does not is a 400 naming the field and the address. Send [] rather than omitting the key.

fields.name: external_mails
fields.description: Addresses outside the group, not validated against any user. Send [] rather than omitting the key: a missing key fails mid-write, after the report row exists, and the server then deletes it again and answers 422.

body.name: project_ids
body.description: PR-NNN identifiers for a cross-project report. Defaults to just the project in the path. Every identifier must resolve or the call is a 400 listing each bad one. More than 60 is a 400; more than one is allowed only for the multi-project report types and, for all of them except Test Case Activity, only with the cross-project feature enabled.

body.name: report_filters
body.description: What the report is scoped to. STRICT ALLOW-LIST of exactly these four keys — any other key, including a typo or an advanced-filter name such as status, priority, assignee, requirements, folder, tc_custom_fields, is a 400 "Filter '<key>' is not supported yet". Nothing is silently dropped.

fields.name: test_runs
fields.description: TR-NNN identifiers, resolved against this project. One that does not resolve is a 400 naming the index, not a partial report.

fields.name: test_plans
fields.description: TP-NNN identifiers, or STP-NNN for a sub-plan. A sub-plan is stored without its kind, so it reads back as TP-NNN.

fields.name: session_ids
fields.description: Exploratory session ids, for the Exploratory Session Summary report. Passed through as given — not identifier-resolved.

fields.name: projects
fields.description: Project scope filter kept alongside project_ids for reports that filter by project rather than span them.

body.name: dynamic_filters
body.description: Saved filter criteria re-evaluated each run, keyed by base entity (test_run / test_case / test_plan). Custom fields and automation_state are accepted; owner, last_executed_by, created_at and updated_at are rejected with a 400. Whatever you send here is NOT echoed back on any read — the report detail always reports dynamic_filters as null.

fields.name: test_run
fields.description: Test-run criteria, e.g. status. owner / last_executed_by / created_at / updated_at inside this object are a 400.

fields.name: test_case
fields.description: Test-case criteria, e.g. custom fields or automation_state.

fields.name: test_plan
fields.description: Test-plan criteria, same rejected keys as above.

capabilities.intent: Set up a new report over a project's test data — either a one-off you will download, or a recurring daily/weekly/monthly schedule that emails chosen people; this saves the report's definition (type, window, scope, recipients) and hands back its SC-NNN identifier, it does not produce any figures
guidance: This returns a report DEFINITION, not report content. The 201 body is the saved configuration echoed back — identifier, type, timeframe, filters, schedule, recipients — and contains no counts, rows or figures at all. Never present it as the report's findings.

Getting the content afterwards is a separate, ASYNCHRONOUS step: request a download for the new SC-NNN and the server answers 202 with a job_id and a status URL, having queued the generation; then poll the matching download-status read until status flips from 'processing' to 'ready' and a file_url appears (pdf or csv only). Nothing in this create waits for that.

The alternative route to content is the v1 report reads (report detail and its section/widget reads), but those take the INTEGER report id and this API never exposes it — SC-NNN is a per-group sequence, so you cannot derive it. Resolve it through the v1 schedules listing, which carries `id` and `identifier` on the same record.

The real required set is only report_type, report_timeframe and report_creation_mode. The published spec additionally marks title, frequency, mail_to and report_filters required — they are not, and title silently defaults to '<report_type>-MM/DD/YYYY'.

Scheduling needs frequency AND frequency_details together, with frequency one of daily/weekly/monthly. Send frequency alone, or frequency:'once', and you get an unscheduled one-off back with a 201 and no warning — check is_scheduled and next_run_at in the response before telling anyone a schedule exists.

Recipients are wired up only for a recurring report: mail_to on a one-off is accepted and then ignored, so nobody is emailed. When you do send it, include BOTH users and external_mails (empty arrays are fine) — a missing key fails after the record is written, and the server deletes the half-built report and answers 422 'Failed to create report'.

Every identifier in the body is resolved before anything is written: an unknown email, TR-, TP- or PR- value comes back as a 400 with field-level errors, and nothing is persisted. Validation errors otherwise arrive as a single 400 message string prefixed 'Validation error.'
