Cross-project: more than one entry in project_ids is allowed only for Test Run Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Summary, Test Plan Detailed Report, Test Case Activity, Requirement Traceability Report and User Workload Report (a 400 otherwise), is capped at 60 projects, and for every one of those except Test Case Activity also needs the cross-project feature enabled for the group — without it the answer is 403 'Operation not permitted'.

The only way back from this call is deleting the report, which is itself irreversible — there is no archive or trash for reports. Re-running a create with the same title does not replace anything: titles are not unique and you get a second report.

capabilities.name: get_report_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all. It is authoritative: the report must belong to this project or the read is a 404, even inside the same group.

path_params.name: report_id
path_params.description: Report identifier in SC-NNN form — the `id` field of the v2 report listing. The route is constrained to SC-\d+, so the integer report id used by the v1 report capabilities gives a routing 404 here, and SC-NNN is a per-group sequence number that cannot be converted to that integer by stripping the prefix.

capabilities.intent: Read one report's setup by its SC-NNN identifier — what it covers (type, time window, the runs/plans/sessions it is scoped to), whether it is on a schedule and when it next runs, who receives it, and whether a generated file exists; configuration only, no figures
guidance: This returns the report's CONFIGURATION, never its data — there is no report_data, no counts and no rows in the response. For the numbers inside a report, either fetch the generated file (request a download for this SC-NNN, then poll the download status until it is ready) or use the v1 report detail / section reads, which take the INTEGER report id this API never exposes; the v1 schedules listing is where SC-NNN and that integer appear together.

Every miss is the same 404 'Report not found': an identifier that does not exist, one from another group, and one that exists but belongs to a different project. A 404 therefore does not mean the report is gone — retry under the project that actually owns it, and for a cross-project report any of its projects will serve it.

`latest_attachment` is NOT this report's attachment. It is the newest generated file anywhere in the project, so it can belong to a different report, and it reports ready:true whenever it is present. Its file_type is a MIME type such as application/pdf, not the 'pdf'/'csv' the spec advertises. Only a download job you started yourself tells you about this report's file.
`dynamic_filters` is hard-coded to null on this read even when the report was created with them; only report_filters reflects configured scope.

report_filters echoes public identifiers rather than the internal ids stored (TR-NNN, TP-NNN, assignee emails). Two caveats: a sub-plan filter comes back as TP-NNN because the sub-plan marker is not kept, and if the upstream identifier lookup fails the values degrade to prefix+raw-id which may not be a real identifier.

`frequency` reads 'once' for an unscheduled report — that is a substitution for a stored null, not something the report was created with. Trust `is_scheduled` and `next_run_at` for whether anything will actually fire.
`project_ids` lists every project a cross-project report covers, and `project_id` is only the owning one.

capabilities.name: list_entity_attachments_v2

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Project identifier in PR-NNN form. The v2 routes constrain this segment to PR-\d+, so a bare integer project id does not match the route at all and never reaches the API.

path_params.name: entity_type
path_params.description: Which kind of parent item to read attachments from. A CLOSED set of exactly these three hyphenated plurals, enforced in the route. Singular or snake_case spellings (test-case, test_case, testcase, test_results) do not match the route and come back as a routing 404 with no JSON body, not a validation error naming the field. Test runs and exploratory sessions are not attachable here.

path_params.name: entity_id
path_params.description: Form depends on entity_type: TC-NNN identifier for test-cases (resolved by identifier lookup; the internal integer case id gives 404 'Test case not found'), the plain INTEGER result id for test-results (no TR- prefix - that is a run), TP-NNN or STP-NNN for test-plans. The route leaves this segment unconstrained, so a wrong form is a 404 from the resolver rather than a 400.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter really is named `p`. `page=2` is not read: you silently get page 1 again. 0 is treated as 1.

query.name: per_page
query.description: Rows per page. Unlike the v2 run and result listings this is a real range, not an allow-list of 30/300 - any value up to 300 is honoured. Above 300 the call is refused with 400 'parameter_error' ('Page limit exceeds the maximum limit of 300'). A non-numeric or absent value is NOT an error: it silently falls back to 30, so a typo quietly shortens your page.

query.name: file_type
query.description: Filter by the attachment's content type, matched as a prefix - `image` keeps every image/* row, `application/pdf` only PDFs. Applied upstream; an unmatched value returns an empty list rather than an error.

query.name: uploaded_by
query.description: Filter by uploader, as the INTERNAL NUMERIC user id - not an email and not a username. The value is coerced with to_i, so a non-numeric value such as an email address becomes 0 and matches nothing while still returning 200. Resolve the user id from a project users read before filtering.

capabilities.intent: List the files attached to one test case, test result or test plan - use this to see what screenshots, logs or evidence are on the item and to get the URL for reading each file
guidance: One route serves all three parent types; entity_type is a closed set of exactly `test-cases`, `test-results` and `test-plans`, spelled hyphenated and plural. Anything else, including the singular or snake_case form, fails to match the route and returns a bare 404 rather than telling you the value was wrong.

entity_id is the trap: it is an IDENTIFIER for two of the three types and an integer for the other. test-cases wants TC-NNN (the internal integer id 404s 'Test case not found'), test-plans wants TP-NNN or STP-NNN, and test-results wants the plain integer result id - the one a v2 test-results listing returns as `id`. There is no route constraint on the segment, so the wrong form always surfaces as a 404 from the resolver, never a 400.

A test-result id that belongs to another project is rejected with 404 'Test result not found' rather than an empty list, so a 404 here means wrong id or wrong project, not an item with no attachments.

Page with `p` (NOT `page`) and `per_page`. per_page defaults to 30 and the real ceiling is 300; ask for 300 directly instead of walking pages of 30. Over 300 is a 400 'parameter_error'; a non-numeric value is silently treated as 30.

Rows are deliberately thin: id, name, size in bytes, created_at and url. Despite what the reference spec shows, this listing carries no content_type, byte_size, checksum or download_url. Read the file straight from `url` - there is no separate download capability for these attachments.

Inline attachments are always included. Images embedded in a description through the rich-text editor come back alongside real file attachments and carry an extra `data_id`, so this count can exceed what the item's attachment panel shows.

Prefer this over the v1 test-case attachments read whenever you hold a TC-/TP- identifier, need a test result's or plan's files, or want paging and file-type / uploader filtering. The v1 read handles test cases only, needs the integer project, folder and case ids, and returns every row in one unpaginated response.
`info` carries page, page_size, count, prev and next - use `count` to decide whether another page is worth fetching instead of paging until you get an empty array.

capabilities.name: search_test_results_v1

query.name: issue_id
query.description: The tracker issue whose linked results you want — the issue KEY as the tracker shows it (Jira 'BUG-123', not a numeric id). Forwarded verbatim with no validation, so a wrong or unknown key comes back as an empty list with success:true, never an error. This is the filter the Jira/ADO issue panel uses.

query.name: issue_type
query.description: Which tracker issue_id belongs to. Send it alongside issue_id — results store the tracker name on each link, so omitting it can match links from another tracker. Trackers the product stores links for: jira, azure, asana, linear, clickup, confluence, figma, devrev, gitlab, github, trello, onedrive, google-drive, sharepoint, zoho, custom. Not validated here.

query.name: priority
query.description: Narrow to results whose case carries this priority. Forwarded verbatim, matched against the project's configured priorities — the out-of-the-box set is low / medium / high / critical, but a project may rename or add values, so resolve the real list rather than assuming. An unmatched value yields an empty list, not an error.

query.name: compact
query.description: Shape switch, compared as a literal STRING against 'false'. Only compact=false expands each row with its test_run and test_case objects; every other value (including omitting it, and including boolean false serialised oddly) gives the lean shape with issues and configuration only. Rows always carry issues and configuration whatever you send.

query.name: include_relations
query.description: Read and then thrown away: the action overwrites it unconditionally from the compact switch before the search runs, on BOTH branches. Asking for a relation here has no effect at all and no error. Use compact=false to get test_run and test_case; there is no way to request any other relation on this endpoint.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER, and the parameter is named `p` — `page=2` is not read and silently returns page 1. A value that is not a strictly positive integer (0, -1, 'abc', or a repeated/array form) is rejected before the action with HTTP 400 {success:false, error:'Invalid Params'}.

query.name: per_page
query.description: NOT a page size — a presence flag, and its value is discarded. Sending per_page at ALL (per_page=100, per_page=1, anything non-blank) SHRINKS the page to 10 rows; omitting it entirely gives 30 rows, the maximum this endpoint can return. Omit it whenever you want the fewest round trips.

query.name: q
query.description: Optional wrapper for the same filters, e.g. q[issue_id]=BUG-123&q[issue_type]=jira. When q is present the flat top-level filters are IGNORED and only q's contents are read, and they reach the search service in a different (query_object) shape. It must be a nested param hash — a JSON-encoded STRING here raises and 500s. p and per_page are still read from the top level. Prefer the flat form.

fields.name: issue_id
fields.description: Same as the top-level issue_id.

fields.name: issue_type
fields.description: Same as the top-level issue_type.

fields.name: priority
fields.description: Same as the top-level priority.

fields.name: compact
fields.description: Same string-literal 'false' switch as the top-level compact.

fields.name: include_relations
fields.description: Overwritten from compact exactly as at the top level; it does nothing.

capabilities.intent: Find test results anywhere in the account without knowing the project, run or case — above all, list every result linked to a tracker issue (a Jira/ADO ticket key) to answer 'what testing covers this bug?', optionally narrowed by case priority
guidance: This is NOT a project read and it takes no project. The action replaces whatever project context arrived with a placeholder before calling the search service, so the search spans every project in the authenticated user's group (account) and is scoped by nothing but your filters and that group. Passing a project_id query param cannot narrow it — a numeric one you lack access to only makes the call 404 before the search runs, and a PR-NNN one is ignored outright.

Use this when the only handle you have is an issue key, or when you need results across projects and runs. When you already know project + run + case and want that case's result history, use the per-case reads (get_test_results_for_test_case / get_test_results_for_test_case_v2) instead — they are scoped, richer, and cannot silently span the account.

Failures are swallowed. An upstream search error is logged and the request STILL answers HTTP 200 with success:true, an empty test_results array and info:null. An empty list is therefore not evidence that nothing matched — treat info:null as 'the search did not run' and retry rather than reporting zero results.

Page with `p`, never `page`, and do NOT send per_page: its value is discarded and its mere presence cuts the page from 30 rows to 10. 30 is the hard ceiling here; there is no way to ask for more, so a large issue's results must be walked page by page.

The only filters that exist are issue_id, issue_type and priority. There is no status, date, project, run, case or assignee filter on this endpoint — anything else you need must be filtered from the returned rows yourself.

Row shape changes with compact. With compact=false you get test_run and test_case objects, and `test_run_id` is then overwritten with the run's TR-NNN identifier string. Without it there are no test_run/test_case objects and test_run_id / test_case_id come from the result mapping as integers — so the same field name carries a different type depending on one query flag. Never assume test_run_id is numeric.

Rows carry no custom fields and no step results, and `links.self` appears only for rows that came back with a project_id. To read a result's custom fields, follow up with the project-scoped single-result reads using the row's project_id and id.

issue_id and issue_type are always forwarded even when absent, so calling with no filters at all is a legal account-wide dump of recent results — expensive and rarely what you want. Send at least one filter.

capabilities.name: list_test_run_test_case_comments_v1

path_params.name: project_id
path_params.description: Numeric project id (the v1 route accepts only digits here, not PR-NNN). Resolve it from the project listing.

path_params.name: test_run_id
path_params.description: Test run identifier as TR-NNN (preferred), or the run's bare integer id. A pair that does not resolve to a case in this run is a 400 'TRTC not found', not a 404.

path_params.name: test_case_id
path_params.description: The test case's NUMERIC id, not its TC-NNN identifier — the route only matches digits, so TC-12 never reaches the API. Take it from the `id` field of a v1 test case read or of a row in the v1 run test-case listing (the TC-NNN is that row's `identifier`).

query.name: mappingId
query.description: Id of the test-case-in-run mapping row (one per configuration the case is mapped to). The spec marks it REQUIRED; the server accepts the call without it and resolves the pair itself, but when a case is mapped to several configurations only this picks the exact cell, and threads differ per cell. Send it when you have it. A value that does not match this run/case pair is a 400.

query.name: p
query.description: PAGE NUMBER — the parameter really is named `p`; `page=2` is ignored and you get page 1 again. Page size is fixed at 30 and cannot be changed. A page past the end does NOT error or come back empty: the server serves the LAST page again, so stop when info.next is null rather than when a page is empty. 0 or a non-number is a 400.

capabilities.intent: List the comments left on a test case inside a specific test run — use this to read the discussion or review feedback on that execution, find who said what and when, or discover a comment's id
guidance: Needs the test-case VIEW permission (a 403 'This action is not permitted for the user' otherwise) AND a paid plan: on a free plan the call still returns HTTP 200 with {success:false, error:'This Feature is only for paid customers'} — check `success` in the body, not the status code.

Three ids in the path, two conventions: project_id and test_case_id are plain INTEGERS (a TC-NNN in the case slot never matches the route), while test_run_id takes the TR-NNN identifier or the bare integer. Get the numeric case id from the `id` field of a v1 test case read or of the v1 run test-case listing.

A run/case pair that does not resolve is a 400 with message 'TRTC not found for given testrun_id:…' — not a 404 — and an automation (Automate/Observability) run is a 400 'Can't comment on automation test'. A test case that does not exist in your group is a bare {success:false} 404.

Comments are threaded per run/case/configuration cell. If the case is mapped to more than one configuration in the run, pass mappingId to pick the cell; without it the server resolves a cell itself and you may read a different thread than the UI shows.

Newest first (by id), 30 per page, no page-size control. `info.count` is the total across pages; walk `p` until `info.next` is null — asking for a page beyond the end silently returns the last page again, so an 'empty page' loop never terminates.

body.example: Failed on Safari 17 only — retest after the fix for TM-1234 lands.

capabilities.intent: Post a comment on a test case within a test run — use this to leave review feedback on an execution, ask the run owner a question, record why a result was marked as it was, or @mention a colleague
guidance:
Send the body as application/json with the nested shape {"comment": {"comment": "

text

"}} — the field is named comment inside an object also named comment. Without a JSON content type the schema check is skipped and the call fails later with a less helpful 400.

capabilities.intent: Kick off no-code (LCNC / Low Code Automation) generation of an automated test for ONE test case — use this when the user wants a manual case automated or re-automated; it queues work in the automation service and returns immediately

message.example: This action is restricted for GRR enabled users

capabilities.intent: Record a reviewer's verdict on test cases that are under review — approve them, reject them, or request changes — for one case or a whole selection in a single call
guidance: Every selected case must currently be 'in_review'. If any is not (the author edited it and it dropped back to pending, or it was already decided) the WHOLE call is refused with 422 {success:false, error_code:'invalid_review_state'} and nothing is applied — re-read the cases and resubmit only the ones still under review.

Needs project setting review_approve ON (else 400 {errors:'Please enable review approve feature ...'}) and a Team or Pro plan (else 422 'Feature not available'). No RBAC permission entry exists for this action beyond project access.

Part 11 e-signature: when project setting part_11_reauth is 'true', every verdict value requires a fresh reauth_token from the re-authentication step (not in this index); missing/expired/reused → 401 {success:false, error_code:'reauth_required'}.

Selections over 100 cases are applied asynchronously: {success:true, async:true, unique_id} with no testCases; re-read to confirm. Below that the updated cases come back inline, plus `comment` (the created comment objects) when a comment was sent.
Cases locked by another bulk operation → 400 {success:false, message:'TestCases in progress with another operation'}.

When the backing store rejects the verdict (e.g. the audit-log write fails) its status is passed through with {success:false, error_code, errors}; the verdict was not applied. Any other failure is a generic 400 {success:false, errors:'An error occurred during bulk approval'}.
Recoverable: a verdict is a tracked review status — the author can edit and resubmit, a reviewer can decide again, and every case keeps version history. Nothing is deleted.
Side effects outside the data: owners get an in-app alert for every verdict, an email too when notify is 'true', and Part 11 projects write an audit-log row.

422.description: Verdict refused: a selected case is no longer under review (error_code invalid_review_state), or the account plan lacks the feature.

error.example: Test case in Pending state cannot be approved. It was modified and moved back to Pending — refresh to review the latest changes.

message.description: Present instead of error/errors on the plan gate ('Feature not available').

capabilities.intent: Check, before exporting test cases to a BDD feature file, that every selected BDD case shares the same Feature and Background text so they can be merged into one file — returns a pass/fail verdict and message, nothing is exported or changed
guidance: Pure check despite the POST: it only reads the selected cases' steps and compares them; no export job, file or record is created. Run it before the real export when the user wants a single merged feature file.

Pass and fail share ONE body shape {success, message}: HTTP 200 + success:true on pass, HTTP 400 + success:false on any failure. Read `message` to tell the failures apart — 'No BDD Test Case(s) selected.' means the selection contained no BDD-template cases at all.

Hard cap: a selection resolving to more than 300 BDD cases is refused with 400, but with the MISLEADING message 'Validation failed. Selected test cases belong to different features or backgrounds.' — the same text as a genuine mismatch. Check the selection size yourself before trusting that message.
Only BDD-template cases are considered: text/step cases in the selection are filtered out silently and a pass says nothing about them.
Comparison is exact after trimming whitespace, on the Feature and Background of each case's FIRST step only.
No RBAC permission is attached to this action; project access and authentication suffice.

ReportType.description:
Report type, sent as its DISPLAY NAME (not a machine slug).

Seven types produce data. `Defects Summary` and `Defects Detailed Report` are
accepted on create/update but have no data branch on the server, so such a report
always reads back with `report_data: null` — never offer them as a way to report
on defects (use `Test Run Summary`, whose sections include `issues_by_priority` /
`issues_by_status`).

Pick by what the user asked about:
  - test cases created / updated / deleted, churn, top creators → `Test Case Activity`
  - run execution + pass rates                                 → `Test Run Summary`
  - per-case results within runs                               → `Test Run Detailed Report`
  - plan-level rollup                                          → `Test Plan Summary`
  - requirement/issue coverage                                 → `Requirement Traceability Report`
  - exploratory sessions                                       → `Exploratory Session Summary`
  - per-user workload                                          → `User Workload Report`

ReportFrequency.description:
Scheduling cadence. Send `frequency` and `frequency_details` TOGETHER, or omit
BOTH — omitting both creates a valid unscheduled, on-demand report.

Two consequences of omitting them: `mail_to` is only persisted for scheduled
reports (recipients on an unscheduled report are silently dropped), and
`next_run_at` stays null.

There is no `once` value — the server's cadence enum is daily/weekly/monthly only.

ReportTimeframe.description:
The window a report covers. Also the value of the `reportTimeRange` query param
on the report-detail read.

The four relative windows compute a date range from "now". `custom` computes it
from `custom_date_range` and **requires** that field — sending `custom` without it
is an unhandled server error, not a 422.

The five remaining values carry no dates; they select entities through
`report_filters` instead:
  `specific_test_runs`  → report_filters.test_runs
  `specific_test_plans` → report_filters.test_plans
  `specific_test_cases` → report_filters.test_cases
  `specific_sessions`   → report_filters.session_ids
  `requirements`        → report_filters.requirements

FrequencyDetails.description:
Shape depends on `frequency` — the server rejects the wrong shape with
"Invalid report frequency", which names `frequency` even when `frequency` itself
was fine and only `day` was missing:

  daily   → { "time": "08:00" }
  weekly  → { "time": "08:00", "day": "monday" }   day = lowercase day name
  monthly → { "time": "08:00", "day": 15 }         day = integer 1-28

`time` is 24-hour `HH:MM`, interpreted as UTC.

is_scheduled.description: True only when a valid frequency and frequency_details pair was supplied.

owner.description: Creator, as email and full_name. No user id is exposed.

mail_to.description: users (email + full_name objects) and external_mails (plain addresses). Populated only for scheduled reports.

report_filters.description: Configured scope echoed back as public identifiers (TR-NNN, TP-NNN, assignee emails). Sub-plans collapse to TP-NNN; values fall back to prefix+internal id if the lookup fails.

dynamic_filters.description: Always null on this surface, whatever was sent at create time.

latest_attachment.description: Newest generated file in the PROJECT, not necessarily this report's: generated_at, file_type (a MIME type such as application/pdf) and ready, which is true whenever the object is present.

id.description: Attachment id. This is the id the delete-attachment capabilities take.

size.description: File size in bytes. Renamed from the stored byte_size field, which is not present under this name here.

data_id.description: Present ONLY on inline attachments (images embedded via the rich-text editor). Its presence is how an inline row is told apart from a real file attachment.

id.description: Result id. Project-scoped single-result reads need this together with project_id.

description.description: Result notes as rich text. User mentions are rewritten to display names in this payload.

created_by_imported.description: Name carried over from an import when the result has no BrowserStack author.

attachments.description: Each entry also carries a human-readable `size` string derived from byte_size.

issues.description: Linked tracker issues. Each entry carries issue_id and issue_type, plus a duplicate `jira_id` mirroring issue_id whatever the tracker actually is.

test_run_results_mapping_id.description: Id of the run/case mapping the result hangs off.

links.description: Present only when the row carried a project_id. Holds `self` only — no custom_fields link on this path.

review_status.description: Present only on comments that were recorded as part of a review verdict.

internal_name.description: Stable machine name (passed, failed, blocked, untested, ...). Use this to compare across projects; ids differ per project.

owner.description: Raw BrowserStack user id of the owner; see owner_details for the person.

folder_path.description: Breadcrumb of the folder the case was in when binned.

updated_by.description: Raw BrowserStack user id of who moved it to the bin; see updator_details.

days_remaining.description: Days left before automatic permanent purge.

TestRunTestCasesV2Response.description: Paginated test cases of a test run. `info` carries the paging counts and reflects any filters applied.

V2TestRunResultSubmitResponse.description: Result submission accepted. The single form returns the written result under `test-result` (or `test-run-step-results` + `overall-result-status` for a step submission). The bulk form returns only `success: true` when everything was accepted, or `success: false` with `status: "PARTIAL"` and per-case `results` when some entries were rejected — still HTTP 200.

success.description: false on a PARTIAL bulk response even though the status is 200.

status.description: Present only when some bulk entries were rejected.

overall-result-status.description: Status rolled up from the submitted step results.

attachments.description: Attachments bound on a multipart submission.

dropped_attachments.description: Files that were uploaded but belonged to an entry that got rejected.

V2BulkResultStatusAcceptedResponse.description: The bulk status change was queued. It says nothing about which cases were changed or whether the work succeeded.

V2TestResultListResponse.description: Recorded results for one test case in one test run, newest executions included as separate entries. Note the key is `test_results` with an underscore, unlike the v1 list's `test-results`.

TemplateListResponse.description: A page of test-case templates with pagination metadata.

TemplateDetailResponse.description: A single test-case template with its full field layout.

TemplateWriteAckResponse.description: Bare acknowledgement of a template write. Carries no template body, so re-read the template to confirm the result.

success.description: True on success. A free-plan refusal also arrives with HTTP 200 but sets this false and adds a message, so check this flag rather than the status code.

V2HistoryListResponse.description: A page of test case revisions, newest first.

history.description: Revision records for the test case, newest first. Note the key is singular `history`, unlike the v1 listing's `histories`.

TestPlanV2Response.description: A single test plan (or sub-plan read through the plan route). No data wrapper — the plan sits at the top level under `test_plan`.

SubTestPlanV2Response.description: A sub-plan returned by the parent-scoped route. The plan sits under `sub_test_plan`, NOT `test_plan`, and its identifier is STP-NNN.

TestPlanV2ListResponse.description: A page of test plans. Rows omit the embedded test_runs preview and links that the single-plan read adds.

TestRunsListV2Response.description: A page of v2 test runs — the shape returned by both the project-wide run listing and a plan's linked-run listing, which share one serializer. success is hard-coded true even when the upstream run fetch failed; in that case test_runs and info are null and the HTTP status carries the failure.

CustomFieldV2DetailResponse.description: A single custom field after a create or edit. The options, assigned_projects, applies_to_all_projects and link_to_future_projects keys are replayed from the request rather than read back from storage, and are omitted when the request did not carry them.

id.description: Numeric field id — the value the single-field read and the field edit take in their path.

field_type.description: Stored type. Always the stored value, never the one sent on an edit.

is_required.description: Whether a test case must fill the field.

default_value.description: Stored default. Null after a create, because a default cannot be set at create time. On a boolean field it is stored as "1" or "0".

place_holder_text.description: Hint text. Absent when the field has none.

options.description: Echo of the options sent in the request, NOT the stored option list. Absent when the request sent none, even if the field has options stored.

applies_to_all_projects.description: Echo of the request flag, defaulting to false — not a statement about the field's stored project links.

assigned_projects.description: Project identifiers echoed back from the request, truncated to the first 30. Absent when the request sent none.

link_to_future_projects.description: Echo of the request flag, defaulting to false.

CustomFieldV2WithDatasetsResponse.description: A single custom field read by id: stored metadata plus references to the datasets that hold its option values. Carries no option values and no real project configuration.

default_value.description: Stored default; "1" / "0" on a boolean field.

place_holder_text.description: Absent when the field has none.

applies_to_all_projects.description: Always false on this read — a placeholder, not the field's real project scope.

link_to_future_projects.description: Always false on this read — a placeholder, not the field's real future-project setting.

dataset_ids.description: Ids of the datasets holding this field's option values and project links. Empty for a field type that has no options.

datasets_url.description: Ready-made link to this field's dataset collection.

dataset_urls.description: Ready-made link per dataset, in the same order as dataset_ids.

V2ReportListResponse.description: Paginated list of a project's report configurations, plus group/project totals for the filtered set.

info.description: Pagination metadata: page, next, prev, count, page_size.

count.description: Total matching rows, not rows on this page.

scheduled_report_count.description: Scheduled reports within the filtered set, across all pages.

total_report_count.description: All reports within the filtered set, across all pages.

V2ReportDetailResponse.description: A single report configuration, returned by the v2 report create (201) and single-report read (200). Carries no report data.

AttachmentListV2Response.description: A page of attachments on one test case, test result or test plan.

TestResultSearchResponse.description: Account-wide test result search page. Always HTTP 200 with success:true — an upstream search failure is swallowed and shows up as an empty test_results array with info null, not as an error status.

success.description: Always true on this endpoint, including when the search itself failed. Do not use it as a success signal.

test_results.description: Matching results, at most 30 per page (10 if per_page was sent at all). Empty both when nothing matched and when the search errored.

info.description: Paging metadata from the search service. NULL when the search failed — that, not the status code, is how you detect the failure.

CommentsListResponse.description: A page of comments on one run/case cell, newest first, fixed 30 per page. info.count is the total across pages; a page past the end repeats the last page rather than returning an empty array.

CommentResponse.description: The comment just posted, wrapped as data.comment. HTTP 200, not 201.

TestRunConfigurationProgressResponse.description: Execution progress of a test run by result status. TWO shapes: when configuration_id was sent the body is {success, overall_progress_by_status_id} and `configurations`/`info` are absent; when it was not, the body is {success, configurations:[...], info} and the top-level `overall_progress_by_status_id` is absent. `info` is the backing service's paging block passed through unchanged (its exact fields are not fixed by this service).

overall_progress_by_status_id.description: Only in the single-configuration form. {} when no results exist for that configuration.

configurations.description: Only in the all-configurations form. One page of the run's configurations, each with its progress attached.

overall_progress_by_status_id.description: Omitted for a configuration with no recorded progress.

info.description: Only in the all-configurations form. Paging metadata from the backing service, passed through as-is.

BinnedTestCasesListResponse.description: A page of binned test cases. Paging lives under `metadata` (total/page/page_size/total_pages), not the usual `info` envelope. Field names follow the backing service's client model; confirm against a live call if a field is missing.

TestCaseReviewOutcomeResponse.description: Outcome of a bulk review submission or verdict. Under 100 cases: the updated cases inline (testCases) — verdicts with a comment also carry `comment`. Over 100: {success, async:true, unique_id} and NO testCases; the change lands in the background.

testCases.description: Updated cases (serialized test case, including review_status and reviewers). Absent on the async path.

comment.description: Verdict only, when a comment was sent: the created comment objects {id, comment, review_status, user{id, full_name, email}, created_at ...}.

async.description: true when the selection exceeded 100 and was queued.

unique_id.description: Identifier of the queued background operation (async path only).

ReauthRequired.description: Part 11 e-signature required: the reauth_token was missing, expired (5 min) or already used. Re-authenticate and resend with a fresh token.

LcncCreateWrapperResponse.description: Wrapper around the automation service's reply. `status` is the upstream HTTP code and `body` is the upstream body as a JSON-encoded STRING to parse (except the 'already in progress' short-circuit, where body is an object {message, title} and status is 'ok'). HTTP 200 outside does not mean success inside — inspect status and body.

status.description: Upstream HTTP status (an integer), or the string 'ok' on the already-in-progress short-circuit.

body.description: Upstream body as a JSON string; typically {status:'submitted'|'failed', message, test_id?, test_version_id?, reason?} on the bulk-pipeline path.

BddExportValidationResponse.description: Verdict of the BDD export pre-check; the same shape is returned on pass (200, success:true) and on every failure (400, success:false) — read message.

message.example: Validation successful. All test cases belong to the same feature and background.

TestRunV2Response.description: The test run, at the top level of the body. The v2 run endpoints do NOT use the `data` envelope the v1 run endpoints use.

TestRunWriteV2Response.description: The updated test run under `testrun` (no underscore between test and run) at the top level. No `data` envelope.

activity.title: Activity feed (audit trail)
activity.description: Group-wide audit trail of who changed what, on which entity, and when.
key_facts: READ-ONLY by design. Activity events are emitted by the system as a side effect of other writes — there is no create, update, or delete, and there never will be. If asked to edit or remove an audit entry, say it is immutable.

HARD 15-DAY WINDOW. The server clamps every query to the last 15 days no matter what you ask for. For anything older, say the history is not retrievable through the API and point to the Test Management UI — do NOT report 'no activity' for an older period, which would be a false negative.

CURSOR pagination, not page numbers. Follow pagination.next_cursor and stop when pagination.has_next_page is false. There is no p param and no info.count, so you CANNOT state a total number of events or jump to a page.
Not project-scoped in the path — it is group-wide. Pass project_id as a QUERY param to narrow it to one project.

starred_only=true restricts to the caller's starred projects. When they have none the response is {events: [], no_starred_projects: true} — that means 'no starred projects', NOT 'no activity'. Check for that flag before reporting emptiness.
The response carries a projects map (project id → metadata) so you can resolve the project an event refers to without extra reads.
Gated by a group feature flag. If the call is refused, report that the activity feed isn't enabled for the group rather than that there is no activity.

attachment.title: Attachments
attachment.description: A file hanging off a parent test case or test result.
key_facts: ai_uploads uploads a file as AI CONTEXT (restricted types, smaller cap) for seeding case content — see create-test-case.
Each blob/attachment row carries an integer id and a url (the file's location) — read the file from that url; there is no dedicated download endpoint.

configuration.title: Configurations
configuration.description: An operating system, browser or device combination that a test run executes against.

custom_field.title: Custom fields & system fields
custom_field.description: A user-defined field on test cases, results or plans, alongside the built-in system fields.
key_facts: A field applies to ONE entity type (TestCase | TestResult | TestPlan) — pick the matching entity_type; project scope is via the integer project id in the path.
A definition write is workspace-wide, not project-scoped: it affects every project the field's datasets link to. Say which projects are affected BEFORE writing.

field_name IS editable via .../update; field_type is SILENTLY immutable — sending a new type returns 200 and changes nothing. Never report a type change as done; a real one means delete-and-recreate, which destroys every stored value.
Update is a full REPLACE: field_name + field_type + is_required must all be present (missing is_required = 400, missing field_name = 500). Read the field first and resend the whole set.
The project-mapping endpoint uses link_projects / unlink_projects — NOT the linked_projects of the create bodies. The wrong spelling is silently dropped: 200, nothing changed.

Three operations destroy stored data across every linked project: deleting a field, deleting an option, and unlinking a project. There is no bin. Count and name the affected projects before asking to proceed.

Don't confuse a DEFINITION with a VALUE. A definition is which attributes exist; a value is what one case holds. Only values are writable here, through the test-case create/update body's custom_fields.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: A named table of variables and rows that drives data-driven execution of a test case.
key_facts: Team Pro plan gated: without it EVERY dataset endpoint returns 422 "Feature not available". A 422 here means NOT-ENTITLED, not a bad payload — say so and stop, don't retry with a different body.

duplicate.title: Duplicate recommendation (AI dedupe)
duplicate.description: A machine-suggested pair of near-identical test cases, for a human to review and merge.

relations.via: links the pair it believes are duplicates

key_facts: There is NO create. Duplicate suggestions are produced by the dedupe pipeline; a caller cannot author one.
Only status=suggested can be read or resolved; already-merged/archived/discarded suggestions return 404. A 404 here usually means 'already handled', not 'never existed'.
source_tc works ONLY for status=merged, and the snapshot may legitimately be absent (404 with error 'Source test case snapshot not available'). Treat that as 'not retained', not as a retryable error.
This list family pages with `page`, not the `p` used elsewhere in the profile.
Dedupe REVIEW is exposed here; TCG test-case GENERATION is not. Don't offer to generate cases.

exploratory_session.title: Exploratory session
exploratory_session.description: An unscripted, charter-driven testing session and the observations recorded during it.
key_facts: session_id and log_id are plain INTEGERS; the parent project takes the INTEGER project id (v1).
Logs hold rich-text HTML sanitised on write (off-project anchor/image links stripped); defects are the issues linked to the session.
Clone runs async when the session has many logs → re-fetch to confirm (see async-jobs).
No convert endpoint: turn session notes into test cases via the create-test-case flow.

filter.title: Saved filter view
filter.description: A saved, named set of filter conditions a user can reapply to a list view.
key_facts: A saved filter view persists a reusable filter: { name, entity, filters, is_project_level }. entity = testcase | testplan | testrun | exploratory_session; filter_id is an integer.
is_project_level scopes the view to the whole project vs. just the creator.

folder.title: Folder
folder.description: A container organising test cases inside a project; folders nest to form a tree.
key_facts: Folder ids are plain INTEGERS (e.g. 54) — never FL-… strings. Nesting is via parent_id (integer, null = root).
mv cross-project and copy run ASYNC ({ success, async, unique_id }) — confirm by re-reading the destination (see async-jobs).

project.title: Project
project.description: The top-level container that owns every folder, test case, run, plan and report.

report.title: Report
report.description: A saved, optionally scheduled analytics view over a project's test data.
key_facts: report_id and schedule_id are INTEGERS; the parent project takes the INTEGER project id (v1).

report_type on create/update is a DISPLAY NAME and the set is CLOSED — exactly these nine: Test Run Summary, Test Run Detailed Report, Test Plan Summary, Requirement Traceability Report, Test Case Activity, Exploratory Session Summary, User Workload Report, Defects Summary, Defects Detailed Report. Never invent one and never substitute a neighbouring type: if the user asks for activity, it is 'Test Case Activity', not 'Test Run Summary'.

Defects Summary and Defects Detailed Report are accepted on create but have no data branch — they always read back report_data: null. For defect counts use Test Run Summary's issues_by_priority / issues_by_status sections instead.

null inside report_data means NOT COMPUTED, not 'no data'. A Test Case Activity report fills its headline counts on a bare read; a Test Run Summary leaves issues_data / test_run_status / test_cases_status / issues_by_priority / issues_by_status null until you name them in sections. Never conclude 'there is no defect or status data' from a null — request the section; an empty payload like {total: 0} is a real finding, null is not. And never answer a 400 on sections by retreating to a bare read.
*_drilldown sections return PAGINATED ROWS, not aggregates — never tally rows into a count; read the aggregate section or report_data.

frequency + frequency_details travel together or not at all; omit both for an unscheduled on-demand report. weekly needs day as a lowercase name, monthly needs day as an integer 1-28. There is no 'once'. report_timeframe: custom REQUIRES custom_date_range.
"Understand a report" = fetch the report + its section/widget data and summarise agent-side; the API returns structured data, not narrative.

result.title: Result
result.description: The recorded outcome of one test case in one run: its status, and who set it.
key_facts: Bodies are wrapped in test_result; set status by NAME (status) or id (status_id) — use a real configured status (see statuses-and-states).

bulk-delete SUCCEEDS PARTIALLY and still returns 200. Authorisation is per id (author OR project admin); ids the caller may not delete come back in `skipped` — and BOTH lists are nested under a top-level `result` key, with `skipped` holding OBJECTS ({id, reason}) not bare ids, so read result.deleted_ids / result.skipped. Not as an error. ALWAYS compare deleted_ids against what you asked for and report the skipped ids — treating 200 as 'all deleted' will misreport.
bulk-delete needs a non-empty result_ids array (400 otherwise) of at most 300 ids (422 beyond) — batch bigger sets yourself.
On the v2 surface a result's status is given by NAME (a status configured for the project, matched case-insensitively); the numeric status_id the v1 surface takes is not accepted there.

Logging a result APPENDS to a test case's result history in that run, so the previous outcome stays readable. A bulk status set REPLACES the case's current outcome in place instead — the overwritten status is not recoverable.

Bulk result writes are queued, not applied inline: a success response means accepted for processing. Per-case outcomes come back as ACCEPTED/FAILED, a partly-valid batch still answers 200 with success:false and status PARTIAL, and a bulk status set reports nothing per case at all — read the results back to confirm.
A project can restrict which review statuses are allowed to log an execution result; cases outside that set are rejected with a REVIEW_STATUS_GATE error rather than being logged.

Result attachments only attach on a multipart upload that carries the files alongside the JSON body; naming filenames in a plain JSON request is accepted and does nothing. Limits are 10 files per result, 100 per request and 50 MB per file, and a result description over 16 KB is truncated, not rejected.

shared_step.title: Shared step
shared_step.description: A reusable block of test steps that many test cases embed by reference.
key_facts: A shared step is embedded by MANY test cases, so editing or deleting it changes every one of them at once. That is the point of shared steps, but it also means a delete is a wide blast radius — say how it is used before changing it.
Reference a shared step from a test case's steps via shared_step_id in test_case_steps — see test-case-authoring.

tag.title: Tag
tag.description: A free-text label on a test case, run or plan, used to group and filter them.
key_facts: Tags are referenced by NAME in filters and on cases; the merge endpoint takes integer source_id/target_id, so resolve ids via the tag reads first.
That body MUST carry custom_fields (send {} when not changing any) — omitting it returns 500 'undefined method each for nil', even though the server's validator lists it as optional.
tags/merge is admin-gated (tags_management flag) — may be unavailable for a group; degrade gracefully and say so.

TAG-OBJECT WRITES ARE NOT EXPOSED. Renaming or deleting a tag project-wide is deliberately out of this profile: the endpoints exist but sit behind the tags_management flag that most groups do not have, and tagging is always driven through the ENTITY. If asked to rename or delete a tag, say it is not available here and point to the Test Management UI.

template.title: Test case template
template.description: A reusable field layout for test cases: which description and property fields appear, in what order, shared by every linked project.
template.id_convention: integer, with no prefix. Discover ids through the template list call rather than guessing them.
key_facts: Templates belong to the workspace, not to a project — one template can be linked to many projects and keeps the same id everywhere. Do not look for them inside a project.

Templates exist for test cases, test results, test plans and exploratory sessions, but only test-case templates can be created or edited here; the older listing can enumerate the other three types and returns test-case templates unless asked for another kind.
Template ids are plain integers with no prefix (not PR- or TR- style). Discover an id from the template list rather than guessing it.
Templates have no version history and no recycle bin: an edit overwrites the previous field layout and a deletion cannot be undone from Test Management.
Disabling a template is the reversible alternative to deleting it — a disabled template stops being offered for new test cases but keeps its fields and project links and can be re-enabled.
Changing a template's field layout changes the fields shown on every test case using it, across every linked project. Say how many projects are affected before writing.
Creating, editing and deleting templates are paid-plan features; on a free plan the call reports failure in the body while still answering 200, and reading templates stays available.

The Review & Approve system fields (reviewers and review status) are hidden from reads on this surface and re-added automatically whenever the property fields are rewritten, so they can be neither seen nor removed here.
A template only affects a project once it is linked to it; creating a template links it to nothing unless linkage is requested.
Failures arrive as a single human-readable message next to a false success flag rather than as a structured error code.

test_case.title: Test case
test_case.description: The unit of test logic: title, preconditions, steps and expected results.
key_facts: A filter is a (key, value) pair and each half fails silently: an unknown KEY is dropped (you get the whole project with success: true), and a wrong-form VALUE matches nothing (count: 0, also success: true). So resolve both — never guess either — and see pagination-and-filtering for the key table and each value's source.

A surprising count means check the FORM, not try another value: 0 on a value the user plainly meant = wrong form, so go resolve ids; filtered count == unfiltered count = the key was dropped. Never take either count from a per_page: 1 call — it returns count: 1 regardless of the real total.
required.fields ADDS joined columns; it does NOT slim a row, so naming fields never buys more rows per page. required.fields=["count"] ALONE is the only value that changes the response.

The compact response has a DIFFERENT envelope: no `success` key ({test_cases, info, filter_details} only — absence of success is NOT failure), info.page_size echoes the server ceiling not your per_page, and filter_details is {} so confirm filter intent before the call.

READING ROWS to show a user: leave per_page at its default and walk p until info.next is null. p advances by per_page and not by what came back, so paging over an incomplete read never recovers the gap.
Paths take INTEGER ids (project + folder + case). The case's TC-NNN comes back as data.test_case.identifier on any read; folder ids are plain integers.
Every successful edit to a test case writes a new version, and an earlier version can be restored — so an edit is recoverable even though nothing offers an undo. Deleting the case is not.

That safety net is plan-gated: below an Enterprise or Team-Pro plan only the last 30 days of versions are visible, and restoring one needs a paid plan — so an older edit may not be recoverable in practice.

The newer v2 project surface addresses a test case by its TC-NNN identifier — or by its third-party identifier in workspaces that issue project-level ids — and does not accept the internal integer id; the older v1 surface is the reverse.

Custom fields on a test case are addressed by their display NAME on the v2 surface and by numeric field id on the v1 surface; a name the project does not define is skipped without any error, so a typo reads back as a successful call that changed nothing.

Priority, status and case type are per-project configurable values, not a fixed vocabulary: send the project's own display value (or its numeric id) and resolve the set from the project's system field values before writing.

test_plan.title: Test plan (and sub-plan)
test_plan.description: A container grouping several test runs, typically for one release or milestone.
key_facts: Paths take the INTEGER plan id. The prefixed identifier (TP-NNN / STP-NNN) is for display; never put it in a v1 path.
The read detail has NO data wrapper: the plan sits under a top-level test_plan key, and test_plan.identifier is the TP-NNN / STP-NNN.
Sub-plans are HIDDEN by default in the list. Without include_sub_plans=true you see only top-level plans, so a sub-plan the user named will look missing.

name IS REQUIRED ON EVERY PLAN UPDATE, including one that only touches test_runs. Omit it and the call is rejected with 400 {success: false, error: 'Invalid Update Params'} however valid the rest of the body is — the server's edit branch is gated on name being present. Read the plan first and echo its current name back unchanged. Only a pure plan_status transition and a reviewers-only edit are exempt. Verified live: {test_plan: {test_runs: [198]}} 400s; adding name makes the identical call succeed.

Run ids in test_runs are the INTEGER uuid from a run read — NOT the run's id field, which is the TR-NNN string on every run endpoint (list, plan's run list, single detail alike). Identifiers are forwarded to the backing service uncoerced and fail upstream (observed 502 Upstream service error). Take uuid, never id.

Linking a run MOVES it: a run belongs to at most one plan, so linking silently unlinks it from the plan that held it, with nothing in the 200 to say so. Read the runs' current membership first and tell the user which plans will lose runs. Verified live.

test_runs accepts an id array OR a bulk-selection object {select_all, de_selected_ids, search_query}. select_all means 'the newest active runs', NOT 'everything matching' — and `filters` is accepted but SILENTLY IGNORED, so a filtered select_all links the whole recent set. Narrow with search_query (name/identifier substring) or send explicit ids. Verified live.
bulk-archive / bulk-retrieve go ASYNC above the bulk threshold and return {success, async: true, unique_id} — the plans are NOT changed yet. Re-read to confirm; see async-jobs.
execution-trend is scoped by EXACTLY ONE of test_plan_id / test_run_id. Both → 400 'Provide either test_plan_id or test_run_id, not both'; neither → 400 'test_plan_id or test_run_id is required'.
execution-trend and linked-sessions-chart-data return chart DATA. There is no insights-widget object to create, update, or delete in this profile.

A plan's status only moves forward, one step at a time: new -> started -> completed. Once completed the plan is FROZEN — even a rename is refused with 'Cannot update completed test plan' — so complete it last.
Plans keep no version history. An overwritten name, description or date is gone for good; there is no prior revision to restore, unlike a test case.

The same plan is addressed two different ways depending on which generation of the API you are on: the newer surface takes the prefixed identifier (TP-NNN / STP-NNN), the older one the numeric id. Carry whichever the capability you picked declares.

On the newer surface a run's plan membership is changed from the RUN, never from the plan: the plan's own edit ignores a list of runs entirely (the older surface accepts one). Linking still moves the run out of whatever plan held it.
On the newer surface a sub-plan's parent is fixed when it is created — there is no re-parenting or promotion to a top-level plan there, and the plan's owner is always whoever created it.

test_run.title: Test run
test_run.description: One execution cycle over a fixed set of test cases.
key_facts: Only test_case_ids / selection / shared_selection put cases in a run. `filters` and `dynamic_filter` are a forward-sync rule, NOT a selection: a create carrying only `filters` returns 200 with ZERO cases, and sets is_dynamic: true even though you did not ask. Verified live.

Dynamic runs match on nine fields only: priority, status, category, owner, automation_status, automation_state, folder, tags, issues. created_at/updated_at are stored and echoed on read but NEVER matched, so a 'last 7 days' dynamic run drops the date window and over-collects forever. Create runs static unless the user explicitly asks for sync.

test_run.run_state is MANDATORY on create and edit (new_run | in_progress | under_review | rejected | done | closed). It is validated before the selection, so a bare 400 'invalid data' means a bad test_run field — NOT a bad selection shape.

A run's `id` FIELD is the TR-NNN STRING, not the integer — on the project list, a plan's linked-run list and the single-run detail alike. The integer lives in `uuid` ({id: 'TR-90', uuid: 198}). Paths tolerate either form, which hides this; bodies and UI paths do not. Carrying `id` into a test plan's test_runs array sends a string that reaches the backing service uncoerced and 502s there. Take `uuid` whenever a run id leaves a read.
Full lifecycle is exposed: create, edit, assign, bulk-assign cases, bulk-edit results, clone, close, delete.
A test run keeps NO version history and has no restore: unlike a test case, an edited name, cleared tag list or removed case cannot be recovered. Confirm before overwriting or removing.
Removing a case from a run deletes the results recorded against it unless the caller explicitly asks to preserve them — the default is to discard.

Changing which cases a run covers is always queued: the call returns an acceptance immediately and the run still shows the old case list for a moment. Re-read the run's cases to confirm, and do not retry on the acceptance.
Every way of editing a run only ever ADDS cases to it. Taking cases out is a separate operation, and only that one can shrink a run.
The newer API generation identifies a run and its project only by their prefixed ids (TR-14, PR-1) and rejects the plain integers the older generation still tolerates.

Listing a project's runs hides closed ones by default. Unless the caller asks to include closed runs, or filters on a lifecycle state, a run count or 'all our runs' answer silently omits every closed run and still looks complete.

Filtering a run listing by owner fails open: an email that matches nobody in the group is dropped from the filter rather than refused, so a misspelled name returns a wider list that reads as a correct answer. Filtering by plan or by date fails closed and errors instead.

Creating a run does not populate it synchronously. The run exists as soon as the call succeeds, but its test cases are attached by background work, so an immediate read of the run's cases can come back empty or short. Re-read rather than retrying the create, which makes a second run.
A run's name is optional at creation: leave it out and the run is named 'Test Run' plus today's date, which is how projects end up with several identically named runs.

Marking a run as an automation run is not something a caller can do at creation — the flag is accepted and discarded, but it still decides which permission is demanded, so asking for it can be refused outright.

user.title: User
user.description: A member with access to a project: who you assign a case to, or set as an owner.
key_facts: WRITE BODIES take the integer: test_case.owner, test_run.owner/assignee_id — send 14.
An unrecognised q key is dropped, not rejected — the server silently omits that condition and returns an unfiltered set that looks like a successful filter. Use the documented key names verbatim.

version.title: Test case version
version.description: A point-in-time snapshot of a test case, for viewing or restoring an earlier revision.
key_facts: Each record carries source (create/update), modified_fields, a modified map (per-field old/new), user and created_at.
diff (compare two versions) and restore require a PAID plan; listing + single-version reads work otherwise. Degrade gracefully.
A plain-language diff summary is agent-side — read the field deltas and describe them; the API returns structured data, not prose.

A revision is addressed two different ways depending on the generation of the read: the older listing hands back a numeric history record id, the newer one identifies a revision only by its position label V1, V2, … with V1 the oldest revision still visible.

Without an Enterprise or Team Pro plan only the last 30 days of a test case's revisions are visible; older ones are absent with no flag saying so, and position labels count only what is visible, so they renumber as old revisions age out.
In the newer payload the editor arrives as updated_by, an email string that is null when the user cannot be resolved in this group, instead of the nested user object the older records carry.

comment.title: Comment
comment.description: A rich-text note a team member posts on a test case, on its execution in a test run, or on a test plan, to discuss it.
comment.id_convention: Plain integer, assigned on creation and returned as `id` on the posted comment. Existing comment ids are not guessable and must be discovered through the comment listing.

relations.via: scoped to the case's execution in

key_facts: A comment can hang off a test case in its folder, off a test case's execution inside a specific test run, or off a test plan. Only the test-run variant is published in this pass; folder-scoped test-case comments and test-plan comments exist in the product but are not exposed here.

Comments are a paid-plan feature. On a free plan every comment call comes back HTTP 200 with success:false and the message 'This Feature is only for paid customers' — the body, not the status, carries the refusal.
Reading and posting comments both need the test-case VIEW permission; no separate comment or write permission exists, so anyone who can see the case can comment on it.
Comments cannot be posted on automation test runs (Automate/Observability-backed), and not on an archived test case; reading an archived case's comments still works.

Mentioning a colleague — via the mention span markup carrying their BrowserStack user id — notifies them immediately, and the run owner is alerted on every new comment. A mention of someone outside the group fails the whole post.
The body is HTML rich text. Whitespace-only or tag-only content is refused; an inline image counts as content. Stored HTML can differ from what was sent (links normalised, mentions rewritten).
Threads are per run/case/configuration cell: a case mapped to three configurations in a run has three separate comment threads, chosen by the mapping id.
Listings come newest first, 30 per page with no page-size control; asking for a page past the end returns the last page again rather than an empty page, so stop when the next-page marker is null.
Posting a comment is recoverable: the author can edit it or delete it afterwards, and deletion hides the comment rather than destroying it. Neither edit nor delete is exposed in this pass.

On each returned comment `edited` is true once it has been changed after posting; the author object's `id` is the internal TM user id (not the BrowserStack user id) and is null for imported comments, which show the original author's name instead.
